files.content: # e2e [e2e](https://tester.army/e2e?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_intro) is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test. ```ts // tests/checkout.e2e.ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/settings/billing'); await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan'); await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro'); }); ``` An agent step that a later assertion verifies records its actions, and the next run replays them with no model calls until the app changes. Tests without agent steps need no model. Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model. ## Quick start ```bash npx e2e init ``` `init` asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The [quickstart](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/quickstart) covers the rest. To see a finished setup in your stack, open [`examples/`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/tree/main/examples): Vite, Next.js, Astro, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, Flutter, and .NET MAUI, each a standalone project with a passing suite. ## Packages | Package | What it does | | --- | --- | | [`e2e`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/e2e) | The SDK, runner, and CLI. | | [`@e2e-dev/web`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/web) | Browser engine: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright. | | [`@e2e-dev/mobile`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/mobile) | iOS and Android engine: simulators and emulators through agent-device. | | [`@e2e-dev/github`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/github) | Reporter that posts results as a pull request comment. | | [`@e2e-dev/kernel`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/kernel) | Kernel hosted browsers for the web engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/lightpanda`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/lightpanda) | Lightpanda, the open-source headless browser, started per run for the web engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/limrun`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/limrun) | Limrun hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for mobile tests. | | [`@e2e-dev/eas`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/eas) | EAS Simulators hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for the mobile engine. | | [`@e2e-dev/smol`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/smol) | smol machines browsers for the web engine: by default, each attempt branches a warm Chromium microVM. | | [`@e2e-dev/decision`](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/decision-models) | Decision-model executors for bounded semantic actions and assertions, and `decisionFilter()`, which leaves out the tests a pull request is unlikely to affect. | | [`@e2e-dev/testmu`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@e2e-dev/testmu) | TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Android emulators, iOS simulators, and real devices for the mobile engine, and hosted Chrome and Edge for the web engine. | ## Documentation [e2e.tester.army/docs](https://e2e.tester.army/docs). The `e2e` package ships every page, so coding agents can read them offline in `node_modules/e2e/docs`. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Questions go to [Discord](https://tester.army/discord). ## Security Please don't open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Follow [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) and report them to [security@tester.army](mailto:security@tester.army). ## Telemetry The CLI sends anonymous usage data, such as which commands and engines run and where runs fail, but no test content, app content, or credentials. Opt out with `npx e2e telemetry disable` or `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`. [Telemetry](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/telemetry) lists every field. ## Status > [!NOTE] > e2e is in active development on the way to 1.0. APIs and config can still > change between minor releases. ## Made by TesterArmy e2e is built by [TesterArmy](https://tester.army/?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_footer), the agentic testing platform that runs natural language tests on web and mobile apps, on every pull request or on a schedule. Apache-2.0.

title: Quickstart
description: Set up e2e with one prompt to your coding agent, or step by step.
icon: "rocket"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/quickstart.png?v=4a3569d569"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/quickstart.png?v=4a3569d569"
---

import { ModelProvider } from './snippets/model-provider.jsx';
import { SetupPrompt } from './snippets/setup-prompt-card.jsx';
import { Video } from './snippets/video.jsx';
import { VideoCard } from './snippets/video-card.jsx';

export const setupPrompt = `Set up e2e end-to-end tests in this project. Docs: \`https://e2e.tester.army/docs/quickstart.md\`

1. Run \`npx e2e init --yes\` (or the pnpm or bun equivalent for this project). It writes a web config using Vercel AI Gateway, an example test, the e2e skill, and MCP config. It installs nothing yet.
2. Read the e2e skill (\`npx e2e guide\` prints it, \`npx e2e guide <topic>\` prints a topic) and follow it for every step below.
3. Point the target at this app. For a web app, set its URL and the command that starts its dev server. For an iOS or Android app, replace @e2e-dev/web with @e2e-dev/mobile and rewrite the example test for the mobile engine.
4. Ask me which model to use for agent steps: a ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode Console, or SuperGrok subscription, an API key, or a local model. Configure it with its provider package. If it needs a sign-in, give me the \`npx e2e login\` command and wait until I confirm.
5. Install dependencies, run the example test, and fix setup errors until it passes.
6. Write one test for the most important user flow in this app, run it, and iterate until it passes.`;

<VideoCard
  id="4_9z6QWShLc"
  title="Getting Started with Agentic e2e in 4 Minutes"
  subtitle="In this video, Kacper takes a simple Next.js app from zero to a working agentic test suite."
/>

## Set up with your coding agent

Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent
in your app's directory:

<SetupPrompt>

<Prompt description={setupPrompt} children={setupPrompt} actions={["copy", "cursor"]} />

</SetupPrompt>

The agent installs the [e2e skill](/coding-agents), so later prompts such as
"add a test for checkout" need no more setup.

<Note>
Use Node.js 24.8 or newer (22.22.3 or newer on Node.js 22). On Windows, run inside WSL. Mobile tests also
need Xcode with an iOS simulator runtime, or the Android SDK with an emulator.
</Note>

## Set up manually

### Run your first test

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create the test project">
  In your app's directory:

  <CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm
  npx e2e init
  ```

  ```bash pnpm
  pnpm dlx e2e init
  ```

  ```bash bun
  bunx e2e init
  ```
  </CodeGroup>

  Choose **Web (Playwright)** or **Mobile (iOS/Android)**, then a
  subscription, a model provider, or **None** for tests without AI. The
  wizard writes a config and an example test, adds dependencies, and offers
  to set up your coding agent. It keeps existing files.

  <Tabs>
    <Tab title="Web">
    Start your app's dev server at `http://localhost:3000`, or set its address
    in `e2e.config.ts`. You can also [let e2e start it](/web#starting-your-app).

    <Accordion title="Example web config and test">
    This config uses Vercel AI Gateway. The wizard configures the provider you chose.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

export default {
  agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast') } },
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' } }],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```ts title="tests/example.e2e.ts"
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { expect } from 'e2e';

test('app opens', async ({ app, browser }) => {
  await app.open('/');
  await expect(browser.locator('body')).toBeVisible();
});
```
    </Accordion>
    </Tab>
    <Tab title="Mobile">
    Run `npx agent-device doctor` to check your setup. The wizard picks iOS
    on macOS and Android elsewhere. The example opens the Settings app.

    <Accordion title="Example iOS config and test">
    This config uses Vercel AI Gateway. For Android, the wizard sets
    `platform: 'android'` and `app: { bundleId: 'com.android.settings' }`.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

export default {
  agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast') } },
  targets: [{ name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios' }), app: { bundleId: 'Settings' } }],
  workers: 1,
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```ts title="tests/example.e2e.ts"
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { expect } from 'e2e';

test('Settings opens', async ({ app, screen }) => {
  await app.open();
  await expect(screen.getByRole('button', 'General')).toBeVisible();
});
```
    </Accordion>

    See [Mobile](/mobile) to use your own app.
    </Tab>
  </Tabs>

  <Accordion title="Use JavaScript instead of TypeScript">
  Rename `e2e.config.ts` to `e2e.config.js` and `tests/example.e2e.ts` to
  `tests/example.e2e.js`. In the config, delete the
  `import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';` line and `satisfies E2EConfig`.
  Then add a JSDoc type and set `tests`:

```js title="e2e.config.js"
/** @type {import('e2e').E2EConfig} */
export default {
  tests: 'tests/**/*.e2e.js',
  // ...the rest of the config, unchanged
};
```

  The example test has no types to remove. Name later tests `*.e2e.js`. See
  [JavaScript](/reference/config#javascript) for type checks and mixing
  JavaScript with TypeScript.
  </Accordion>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Run the example">
  <CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm
  npx e2e run
  ```

  ```bash pnpm
  pnpm exec e2e run
  ```

  ```bash bun
  bunx e2e run
  ```
  </CodeGroup>

  e2e downloads a browser or boots the simulator or emulator, checks that
  the app opens, and prints the result. The example makes no model calls,
  so it needs no sign-in or API key.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Video>
  <video src="/images/init.mp4" aria-label="npx e2e init asks for an engine, a model gateway, and coding agent setup, then lists the files it will write." muted loop playsInline controls />

  `npx e2e init` asks a few questions, then shows every change before it writes anything.
</Video>

### Use a subscription or API key

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Subscription">
  | Plan | How to connect |
  | --- | --- |
  | ChatGPT Plus or Pro | `npx e2e login openai` |
  | GitHub Copilot | `npx e2e login github-copilot` |
  | OpenCode Console (OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go) | `npx e2e login opencode-console` |
  | SuperGrok or X Premium+ | `npx e2e login spacexai` |
  | Claude Max or Team (Claude Code) | API key from the plan's monthly API credits. See [Claude Max or Team](/subscriptions#claude-max-or-team). |

  Copilot uses your GitHub CLI login if you have one. See
  [Subscriptions](/subscriptions).
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="API key">
  Select your provider. Install its package and set the variables it reads,
  if any, in the terminal where you run e2e.

  <ModelProvider show="select" />

  <ModelProvider show="install" />

  <ModelProvider show="env" />

  The wizard writes the config for Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and
  OpenAI-compatible endpoints. For another provider, replace the model import
  and `model` value in `e2e.config.ts`, and use `agent` as `agents.default`:

  <ModelProvider show="model" />

  See [Models](/models) for local models and more options.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Add an agent step

Give `agent.act` one [atomic goal](/core-concepts#goals) per call, then
check the result. Adapt the example to a flow in your app:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Web">
```ts title="tests/agent.e2e.ts"
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { expect } from 'e2e';

test('a visitor signs up for a trial', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => {
  await app.open('/');

  await agent.act('sign up for a free trial as {name} with email {email}', {
    params: { name: 'Ada Lovelace', email: 'ada@example.test' },
  });

  await agent.assert('the welcome screen greets Ada by name');
  await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('trial');
});
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Mobile (iOS)">
```ts title="tests/agent.e2e.ts"
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { expect } from 'e2e';

test('the agent opens General', async ({ agent, app, device }) => {
  await app.open();
  await agent.act('open {section} settings', { params: { section: 'General' } });

  await agent.assert('the General settings screen is showing');
  await expect(device.locator('role=navigation-bar id=General')).toBeVisible();
});
```

  `app.open()` launches the app fresh. Without it, a test starts where the
  previous one left the device. `device.locator` takes
  [agent-device selectors](/mobile#the-device-fixture).
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

`params` fill the goal's placeholders. `agent.assert` judges the screen.
`expect` checks an exact value.

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e run tests/agent.e2e.ts
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm exec e2e run tests/agent.e2e.ts
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e run tests/agent.e2e.ts
```
</CodeGroup>

If you chose **None** in the wizard, [add a model](/models) first. Add
`--headed` to watch a web test. Add `--no-cache` to skip cached actions.

### Configure the project

`e2e.config.ts` holds the options. These are the ones most projects change
after `init`:

| To | Set | See |
| --- | --- | --- |
| point at your app | `app.url`, or `app.bundleId` on mobile | [The app under test](/reference/config#the-app-under-test) |
| start the app with the run | `app.command` | [Starting your app](/web#starting-your-app) |
| use a model | `agents.default.model` | [Models](/models) |
| test several browsers or devices | one `targets` entry each, with a `name` | [targets](/reference/config#targets) |
| give tests more time | `timeout`, `actionTimeout`, `assertionTimeout` | [timeout](/reference/config#timeout) |
| retry failed tests | `retries`, `1` in CI | [retries](/reference/config#retries) |
| run tests in parallel | `workers`, `1` in CI | [workers](/reference/config#workers) |
| pick the test files | `tests` | [tests](/reference/config#tests) |
| keep traces and videos | `trace`, `video` | [Recording](/reference/config#recording) |
| write a JUnit report | `reporters: ['list', 'junit']` | [reporters](/reference/config#reporters) |
| sign in and pass API keys | `credentials`, `secrets` | [Signing in](/authentication) |
| write the replay cache in CI | `cache: 'read-write'` | [Caching](/cache) |

<Accordion title="Example config with common options">
```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

const app = {
  url: process.env.APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'], reuseExisting: true },
};

export default {
  agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast') } },
  targets: [
    { name: 'chromium', engine: web({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } }), app },
    { name: 'firefox', engine: web({ browser: 'firefox' }), app },
  ],
  timeout: 180_000,
  workers: 4,
  reporters: ['list', 'junit'],
  video: 'retain-on-failure',
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

`--target firefox` runs one target. Targets that share one `command` share
one server process.
</Accordion>

title: Coding agents
description: Give a coding agent the skill, a live app session, and reports it can use to write and debug tests.
icon: "robot"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/coding-agents.png?v=c6990935d7"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/coding-agents.png?v=c6990935d7"
---

A coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor can write, run, and
debug e2e tests. It learns e2e from the skill, uses the app through the
`e2e mcp` server, and reads the trace page of a failed test.

## Install the skill

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e init
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm dlx e2e init
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e init
```
</CodeGroup>

| Path | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `.agents/skills/e2e/` | Agents that read `.agents/skills` |
| `.claude/skills/e2e/` | Claude Code. A symlink to `.agents/skills/e2e/` when both are installed. |

The copy holds `SKILL.md` and topic references. After you upgrade e2e, with
[`e2e upgrade`](/reference/cli#e2e-upgrade) or your package manager, run
`init` again to update it. Without `init`, `npx skills add tester-army/e2e`
installs the skill, and `npx e2e guide [topic]` prints it from the
installed package. The plugin below installs all three e2e skills for
every project.

`init` leaves your project instructions unchanged. For agents that need a
pointer, add this line:

```md title="AGENTS.md"
End-to-end tests use e2e; read .agents/skills/e2e/SKILL.md before writing or running one.
```

The package also ships these docs as `.mdx` pages for offline reading, in
`node_modules/e2e/docs` in a single-package project. A link such as
`/reference/cli` is `docs/reference/cli.mdx`.

<Accordion title="Install the Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor plugin">

The e2e repository is a plugin marketplace for Claude Code and Codex, and
for Grok Build, which reads the Claude Code files. Cursor loads the plugin
from its local plugins folder:

<CodeGroup>
```bash Claude
claude plugin marketplace add tester-army/e2e
claude plugin install e2e@e2e
```

```bash Codex
codex plugin marketplace add tester-army/e2e
codex plugin add e2e@e2e
```

```bash Cursor
repo=$(mktemp -d)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/tester-army/e2e "$repo"
mkdir -p ~/.cursor/plugins/local
rm -rf ~/.cursor/plugins/local/e2e
cp -R "$repo/plugins/e2e" ~/.cursor/plugins/local/
```
</CodeGroup>

Start a new session. In Cursor, run **Developer: Reload Window**. On Cursor
Teams and Enterprise, local plugins need the admin setting **Allow Local
Plugin Imports**, or an admin imports `tester-army/e2e` as a team
marketplace. The plugin adds the
`e2e`, `create-verification-skill`, and `migrate-to-e2e` skills, not the
npm package or the MCP server. Invoke the other two under the plugin's
name, `/e2e:<skill>` in Claude Code and `$e2e:<skill>` in Codex, and as
`/<skill>` in Cursor.

The plugin's version follows e2e releases. To update it, run these and
start a new session. In Cursor, run the commands above again.

<CodeGroup>
```bash Claude
claude plugin marketplace update e2e
claude plugin update e2e@e2e
```

```bash Codex
codex plugin marketplace upgrade e2e
```
</CodeGroup>

</Accordion>

## Let the agent use the app

`e2e mcp` gives the agent a live session on your app. It checks each
locator against the screen before it writes the test, and checks its own UI
changes. `init` registers the server. See [MCP server](/mcp-server) for setup and
prompts.

## How an agent writes and runs a test

The skill tells the agent to read the config and an existing test first.
For known fields and exact values, the agent uses `screen`:

```ts title="tests/checkout.e2e.ts"
import { test, expect, credentials } from 'e2e';

test('a signed-in user reaches checkout', async ({ screen, app, agent }) => {
  const user = credentials.user('customer');
  await app.open('/login');
  await screen.getByLabel('Email').fill(user.username);
  await screen.getByLabel('Password').fill(user.password);
  await screen.getByRole('button', 'Sign in').click();
  await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Welcome back')).toBeVisible();

  await agent.act('Add the cheapest item on the page to the cart');
  await expect(screen.getByRole('status', 'Cart')).toHaveText('1 item');
  await agent.act('Open the cart');
  await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Your cart')).toBeVisible();
});
```

- **One `agent.act` per [atomic goal](/core-concepts#goals), then an
  `expect`.** The `expect` fails when the agent did the wrong thing. A
  locator matcher, or another
  [verification check](/cache#when-a-recording-is-written), also lets the
  cache replay the step.
- **No sleeps.** Locators poll, actions wait for their target, and `expect`
  retries until its timeout.
- **Secrets through `credentials.user(name)`.** Declare them in the config.
  Never write them in a test.

While it iterates, the agent runs only the test it works on, by the line
its `test(` opens on. With `--action-timeout 5000`, a wrong locator fails
after 5 s instead of 30 s:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts:3 --action-timeout 5000
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm exec e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts:3 --action-timeout 5000
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts:3 --action-timeout 5000
```
</CodeGroup>

The agent fixes CLI, config, and collection errors before it runs again.
It doesn't edit cache recordings.

The agent keeps the replay cache on, so a goal whose check passed replays
without model calls. It turns retries off, since a retry runs every goal
live. When the test passes, the agent drops `--action-timeout` and runs it
one time with `--no-cache` to check that the live agent reaches every
goal. See
[Rerun a test while you fix it](/cache#rerun-a-test-while-you-fix-it).

## How an agent reads a failure

By default ([`trace`](/reference/config#trace)), a run writes a trace page
for each failed, timed-out, interrupted, or flaky test, to the test's
directory under `.e2e/results/`. `.e2e` is the default `output`. The
terminal names the page under each failed test, as
`❯ trace .e2e/results/<test>/trace.md`.

The agent reads that page, not `.e2e/report.json`, which holds the same
facts for [scripts](/debugging). The page has the failing line and every
step with what it did: the node an action hit, the values an assertion
read, the cache's decision, console errors, and failed requests. It also
has the agent's last turns and the screen at the failure.

The agent fixes the test from that evidence. It fixes every line the
evidence covers, not only the failing one. A test stops at its first failed
step, so the agent also checks the lines after it before the next run.

To see a screen the page doesn't show, the agent opens it in an MCP session
by the shortest way, such as its URL on the web. It doesn't walk the flow
again from the start.

For model-call details, the agent adds `--ai-trace` and reads the trace
with [unbox-ai](/debugging#agent-steps). Pair it with `--no-cache` to
capture every model call in the flow. Don't open the raw trace in an
agent's context. It repeats prompts and can be several megabytes.

## Generate a verification skill for your app

The e2e skill teaches the runner, not your app. The
`create-verification-skill` skill writes a project-local
`.agents/skills/verify-<app>/` skill that does, and tests it one time
before it hands over.

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill create-verification-skill
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm dlx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill create-verification-skill
```

```bash bun
bunx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill create-verification-skill
```
</CodeGroup>

Then ask the agent for `/create-verification-skill`.

<Accordion title="What the generated skill holds">
- Launch and doctor commands from your config.
- The two ways to drive the app: a live `e2e mcp` session and a test.
- The evidence a proof keeps.
- A feature map with one `e2e explore` charter for each feature, so a
  [bug bash](/bug-bash) fans out from the map.

The generated skill says only what is true of your app and links to the e2e
skill for the rest. It is based on
[create-verification-skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack/skills/create-verification-skill)
from poteto's pstack, with e2e in place of a hand-rolled harness.
</Accordion>

## Migrate an existing suite

The `migrate-to-e2e` skill moves a Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Detox,
or Maestro suite to e2e one slice per session. The old suite keeps
running beside the new tests, so you can stop after any session.

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill migrate-to-e2e
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm dlx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill migrate-to-e2e
```

```bash bun
bunx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill migrate-to-e2e
```
</CodeGroup>

Then ask the agent for `/migrate-to-e2e`. It ports the slice you pick and
runs each ported test three times on every target. A `MIGRATION.md` file
records progress for the next session. Optionally, the agent plants a temporary bug
in the app, such as a wrong checkout total, and checks whether both
suites fail on it. The agent deletes an old test only when you confirm. It first reads the migration guide for your runner:
[Playwright](/migrate/playwright), [Cypress](/migrate/cypress),
[Selenium](/migrate/selenium), [Detox](/migrate/detox), or
[Maestro](/migrate/maestro).

title: MCP server
description: Let your coding agent use your app and check its own work.
icon: "plug"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/mcp-server.png?v=17998906c0"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/mcp-server.png?v=17998906c0"
---

`e2e mcp` gives a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor a live
session on your app, on web, iOS, or Android. The agent sees the screen,
acts on it, and checks its work.

## Why it matters

| Task | Without `e2e mcp` | With `e2e mcp` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Write a test | Guesses locators, runs, fails, guesses again | Copies a checked test line from each action it takes |
| Change the UI | Done when it compiles | Opens the page and checks the result |
| Reproduce a bug | Guesses from the code | Follows the steps in the app |
| Show a change in a PR | Describes it | Records a video |

The server needs no model.

## Set it up

`e2e init` offers to register the server in `.mcp.json` (Claude Code) and
`.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor). By hand:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Claude Code">
    <CodeGroup>
    ```bash npm
    claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- npx e2e mcp
    ```

    ```bash pnpm
    claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- pnpm exec e2e mcp
    ```

    ```bash bun
    claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- bunx e2e mcp
    ```
    </CodeGroup>
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Codex">
    Add the server to `.codex/config.toml`, trust the project, and start a
    new session:

    ```toml title=".codex/config.toml"
    [mcp_servers.e2e]
    command = "npx"
    args = ["e2e", "mcp"]
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Cursor">
    Add the server to `.cursor/mcp.json`. Other clients that read an
    `mcpServers` map take the same block.

    ```json title=".cursor/mcp.json"
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["e2e", "mcp"] }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

A session starts the target's app command, if it has one.

## Ask the agent

- "Add a Remember me checkbox to the login form. Check it in the app with e2e."
- "Write a test for checkout. Check every locator in the app first."
- "Reproduce issue #123 in the app and record a video."

Add "headed" to watch a local browser or simulator.

## How it writes a test line

Each action in a session answers with the test line that repeats it. The
line's locator matched that control alone on the live screen:

```text wrap
Tapped #n31.
Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Sign in").tap();
```

`test_lines` returns every line so far, in order, as a draft test body. The
agent pastes it into a test and adds the assertions. See
[`test_lines`](/reference/mcp#test_lines) for how a line is built.

## How it checks a locator

A locator guessed from the source fails in the session, not in a test run:

```text wrap
0 nodes match getByLabel("Email").
A test using this locator would fail with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND. ...

1 node matches getByRole("button", name: "Sign in").
Use: screen.getByRole("button", "Sign in")
```

## Run tests next to a session

A session doesn't run tests and writes no test results or cache
recordings. The agent runs tests with `e2e run` and, when a run can go
beside the session, keeps the session open between runs. After a failed
run, it goes to the failing screen in that session instead of opening a
new one.

On web, a run next to a session depends on the target's `app`:

| Target's `app` | A run while a session is open |
| --- | --- |
| No `command` | Both use the app you started. |
| `url` on port [`0`](/web#let-the-runner-pick-the-port) | Each starts its own copy of the app. A dev server that runs one copy per directory, such as `next dev`, fails the run. |
| `command` with [`reuseExisting: true`](/web#starting-your-app) | The run uses the app the session started. When the session closes, also during a run, that app stops. |
| `command` on a fixed port, without `reuseExisting` | Fails with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`. |

When `CI` is set, e2e ignores `reuseExisting`, and the run fails as on a
fixed port. Close the session before a run that would fail. On mobile, run
on a device no session uses.

## Run several agents

Each agent, subagents included, opens its own session with its own browser
or device, up to four by default. On mobile, give each session its own
target.

## Secrets

`type_secret` fills a secret without showing it to the agent. After a
secret is filled, the session stops returning screenshots.

<Warning>
Videos from `start_recording` are not masked.
</Warning>

title: Continuous integration
sidebarTitle: Setting up CI
description: Run e2e on GitHub Actions, EAS Workflows, Bitrise, Codemagic, or any CI service that runs Node.
icon: "rotate"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/ci.png?v=01be716140"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/ci.png?v=01be716140"
---

e2e runs on each CI service that can run Node 24.8 or later (22.22.3 or
later on Node 22). Each job installs the dependencies, starts the app or a
device, runs `npx e2e run`, and uploads `.e2e/`.

## Pick your CI service

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="GitHub Actions" icon="/images/integrations/github-actions.svg" href="/ci/github-actions">
    Web and mobile workflows. Post the results as a pull request comment.
  </Card>
  <Card title="EAS Workflows" icon="/images/integrations/expo.svg" href="/ci/eas-workflows">
    Build an Expo app on EAS, then run iOS and Android tests on it.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Bitrise" icon="/images/integrations/bitrise.svg" href="/ci/bitrise">
    iOS and Android workflows with the Bitrise steps for simulators and emulators.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Codemagic" icon="/images/integrations/codemagic.svg" href="/ci/codemagic">
    iOS and Android workflows on Mac mini and Linux instances.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

For another CI service, copy the [GitHub Actions](/ci/github-actions)
workflow. To lease browsers or devices from a hosted service, see
[Hosted browsers and devices](/integrations).

## Upload the reports

Upload `.e2e/` at the end of each job, also when a test fails. It holds:

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `report.json` | The run report, from each run that reaches its tests |
| `junit.xml` | With the `junit` reporter (`--reporter list,junit`): the results, the tests a [test filter](/filters) left out as skipped, and startup failures such as `APP_UNREACHABLE` in a `run` suite |
| `results/` | The trace pages, screenshots, and screen dumps of each test. With `--video`, also a video for each target whose engine can record |

Point the test-report integration of your CI service at `.e2e/junit.xml`.
The [`output`](/reference/config#output) option moves `.e2e/`.

## Model credentials

Give the job the credential your provider needs, such as
`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (see [Models](/models)). Tests that never use `agent`
need none.

<Warning>
Each job that has the key gives it to the code it runs: tests, config, and
dependencies. Give the key only to builds of branches you trust. Run
untrusted pull request code with no secrets and no write tokens. See
[Security](/security).
</Warning>

Keep keys in CI secrets, and set spending limits where you can. GitHub does
not give secrets to pull requests from forks.

## What CI changes

CI mode is on when `CI` has a value other than an empty string, `0`, or
`false`. To get these defaults locally, run `CI=1 npx e2e run`:

| Setting | Local | CI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retries` | `0` | `1` |
| `workers` | half your cores | `1` |
| `cache` when unset | `read-write` | `read-only` |
| `.only` | allowed | rejected with `ONLY_IN_CI` |
| `command.reuseExisting` | honored | ignored, with a notice |

To change the worker and retry defaults, use flags:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e run --workers 4 --retries 0
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm exec e2e run --workers 4 --retries 0
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e run --workers 4 --retries 0
```
</CodeGroup>

To send no [telemetry](/telemetry#in-ci) from CI, add
`E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'` to the `env` of the job.

## Mobile jobs

Without a [hosted device service](/mobile#hosted-devices), each platform
needs its own machine, build, and device:

| | iOS | Android |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Machine | macOS with Xcode and a simulator runtime | Linux with KVM (nested virtualization) |
| Build | Release simulator `.app`, no signing | Release `.apk` |
| Device | A booted simulator | A booted emulator |

Make a Release build on both platforms. A React Native or Expo debug build
loads its JavaScript from Metro, which these jobs don't start, so it opens
on an error screen. The examples use a React Native project with `ios/` and
`android/` in the repository. For an Expo project without them, run
`npx expo prebuild` first.

Install the build, then run the suite:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
# iOS
xcrun simctl install booted path/to/MyApp.app
npx e2e run --target ios --reporter list,junit

# Android
adb install -r path/to/app.apk
npx e2e run --target android --reporter list,junit
```

```bash pnpm
# iOS
xcrun simctl install booted path/to/MyApp.app
pnpm exec e2e run --target ios --reporter list,junit

# Android
adb install -r path/to/app.apk
pnpm exec e2e run --target android --reporter list,junit
```

```bash bun
# iOS
xcrun simctl install booted path/to/MyApp.app
bunx e2e run --target ios --reporter list,junit

# Android
adb install -r path/to/app.apk
bunx e2e run --target android --reporter list,junit
```
</CodeGroup>

The commands assume two targets named `ios` and `android`, each a
`mobile()` engine with the app's `bundleId`. See
[Point at your app](/mobile#point-at-your-app). To let the suite install the
build, set `app.appPath` and call `device.installApp()`.

These rules apply on each service:

- **One job for each platform.** Run `--target ios` on a Mac and
  `--target android` on Linux with KVM. Hosted Macs use Apple Silicon,
  which can't nest virtualization, so the Android emulator doesn't start
  on them.
- **Boot the device in its own step.** With no device booted, the engine
  asks agent-device to boot one, but a new Linux runner has no emulator
  image. A separate step also tells a failed boot from a failed test.
- **Pin the iOS runtime.** A simulator picked by name (`iPhone 17`) runs
  the image's default iOS, and the accessibility tree changes between iOS
  releases. A runner image update can then fail a locator assertion with
  no change in your code. The examples create a simulator on a named
  runtime and boot it by UDID. Replace `iOS-26-5` with a runtime the image
  has (`xcrun simctl list runtimes`).
- **Cache `~/.agent-device`.** agent-device builds its XCUITest runner
  there the first time it drives a simulator.
- **Replay local recordings.** The replay cache key holds the app, not the
  device, so a step recorded on your simulator replays on the CI one.
  [Commit the replay cache](/cache#commit-the-replay-cache).

## Gate pull requests

Each non-zero exit fails the job, a failed agent step included. To block
merges on a failed run, make the e2e job a required check.
[Debugging a run](/debugging#read-the-failure) lists each exit code and
whether rerunning the job can help.

To keep the checks predictable:

- Give each `agent.act` one [atomic goal](/core-concepts#goals). Then
  check its result with a locator assertion or `agent.assert`.
- [Commit the replay cache](/cache#commit-the-replay-cache). A replayed
  `agent.act` makes no model call. With the built-in agent, a cache miss, a
  hand-off, and every agent judgment (`agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`,
  `agent.extract`) call the model.
- Watch for flaky tests. The report marks a test that passes only on the
  CI retry as flaky.
- Add `--max-failures <n>` to stop the run after that many failed tests, so
  a broken deploy doesn't spend a model call on each remaining step. The job
  exits 1.
- Add `--max-duration <ms>` to limit test-running time; the clock starts
  when tests start, not during app startup. The job exits 1.

## Run only affected tests

On a pull request, pass `--changed-since` so a [test filter](/filters) can
leave out the tests the change is unlikely to affect. Without the flag, as
on `main`, the whole suite runs. See
[Add the decision filter](/filters#add-the-decision-filter).

## Sharding

`--shard <index/total>` runs one slice of the suite. Every job runs the
same command with its own index, and every machine slices the suite the
same way. A shard with no test fails with `NO_TESTS`. If a matrix can have
more shards than tests, add `--pass-with-no-tests`. The
[CLI reference](/reference/cli#flags) has the slicing rules.

On GitHub Actions, a matrix runs one job for each shard:

```yaml
jobs:
  e2e:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      # ...
      - run: npx e2e run --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3 --reporter list,junit
```

Upload each shard's `report.json` and `junit.xml` under a name with the
shard index. e2e can't merge shard reports yet.

## Rerunning failures

`--last-failed` runs only the tests that didn't pass in the previous run,
read from `report.json` in the output directory. Run it in the same step as
the first run:

```yaml
      - run: npx e2e run || npx e2e run --last-failed
```

The rerun keeps the first run's artifacts and writes its own under
`rerun-<n>/` in each test's directory, so one upload holds both. The
[CLI reference](/reference/cli#flags) lists what counts as not passed.

A separate job has no report on its runner. Download it into the output
directory first, or rerun the failed job.

export const setupPrompt = `Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs this project's e2e tests. Docs: \`https://e2e.tester.army/docs/ci/github-actions.md\` and \`https://e2e.tester.army/docs/ci.md\`

1. Read both pages. Use the web workflow for web targets and the iOS and Android workflow for mobile targets.
2. Adapt the workflow to this project: package manager, Node version, how the app starts or builds, and the app paths.
3. For a mobile job, replace the iOS runtime with one the runner image has, and keep it pinned.
4. List the repository secrets the workflow reads, such as the model key, and ask me to add them.
5. After I push, read the job log and fix errors until the job passes.`;

These two workflows run web targets, and iOS and Android targets. For CI
defaults, model keys, and exit codes, see [Continuous integration](/ci).

<SetupPrompt>

<Prompt description={setupPrompt} children={setupPrompt} actions={["copy", "cursor"]} />

</SetupPrompt>

## Web

This workflow runs deterministic and agent tests in one job. It assumes a
config [command](/web#starting-your-app) that starts the app, and AI
Gateway for the model calls. The model key and user credentials come from
repository secrets:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/e2e.yml" expandable
name: e2e

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install browsers
        run: pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Run e2e
        run: npx e2e run --reporter list,junit
        env:
          APP_URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Upload report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: e2e-report
          path: |
            .e2e/report.json
            .e2e/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts
          path: .e2e/results
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7
```

`npx e2e` runs the version the lockfile installs. The
[install command](/reference/web#installing-browsers) downloads the browsers
for the engine's pinned Playwright version, with their system libraries. A
test that passed on retry keeps its failed attempt's evidence in the upload.

## iOS and Android

This workflow runs one job for each platform and follows the rules in
[Mobile jobs](/ci#mobile-jobs). Any build command that writes a simulator
`.app` without starting the app can replace `xcodebuild`. For Expo,
`npx expo run:ios --configuration Release --device generic --no-bundler --output build/ios`
builds without a simulator and writes the `.app` under `build/ios`.

```yaml title=".github/workflows/e2e-mobile.yml" expandable
name: e2e mobile

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  ios:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: pod install
        working-directory: ios

      - name: Build for the simulator
        run: |
          xcodebuild -workspace ios/MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp \
            -configuration Release -sdk iphonesimulator \
            -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
            -derivedDataPath build
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.agent-device
          key: agent-device-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Boot a simulator and install the app
        run: |
          UDID=$(xcrun simctl create e2e "iPhone 17" com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimRuntime.iOS-26-5)
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$UDID" -b
          xcrun simctl install "$UDID" build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app

      - run: npx e2e run --target ios --reporter list,junit
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: e2e-ios
          path: .e2e
          if-no-files-found: warn

  android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: npm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      # React Native and Expo templates sign release builds with the debug keystore.
      - name: Build the APK
        run: cd android && ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease

      - name: Run on an emulator
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 36
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          profile: pixel_7
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
            npx e2e run --target android --reporter list,junit
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: e2e-android
          path: .e2e
          if-no-files-found: warn
```

The emulator runner action runs each `script` line in a new shell and stops
the emulator when the step ends. Install and run in the same step.

This repository's own
[`mobile.yml`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/.github/workflows/mobile.yml)
adds a cached Expo build per native fingerprint, two simulators for two
workers, and a `--last-failed` rerun.

## Pull request comments

Add the [`@e2e-dev/github` reporter](/github) to post each job's results as
one pull request comment, updated on a rerun and copied to the job summary.

The job needs `pull-requests: write` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the test step's
env; the workflows above are read-only. See [Setup](/github#setup). A fork's
`pull_request` run gets a read-only token, so nothing is posted
([why](/github#when-nothing-is-posted)).

title: Telemetry
description: What the CLI sends, what it never sends, and how to turn it off.
icon: "chart-line"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/telemetry.png?v=723dc5172f"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/telemetry.png?v=723dc5172f"
---

The `e2e` CLI sends anonymous usage data: which commands, engines, and
features people use, and where runs fail. Telemetry is on by default. It
sends counts and versions, never test content, app content, or credentials.

## Opt out

Any one of these turns telemetry off:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e telemetry disable   # saved in ~/.config/e2e/telemetry.json
export E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1          # for a shell or a CI job
export DO_NOT_TRACK=1                    # the cross-tool convention
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm exec e2e telemetry disable   # saved in ~/.config/e2e/telemetry.json
export E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1          # for a shell or a CI job
export DO_NOT_TRACK=1                    # the cross-tool convention
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e telemetry disable   # saved in ~/.config/e2e/telemetry.json
export E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1          # for a shell or a CI job
export DO_NOT_TRACK=1                    # the cross-tool convention
```
</CodeGroup>

The environment variables win over the saved setting. `e2e telemetry enable`
reverses a saved `disable`. `e2e telemetry` prints the status and, when off,
the reason. The preferences file is under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/e2e/` when that is
set, and `%APPDATA%\e2e\` on Windows.

A `disable` also stops commands already running in another terminal. Nothing
is sent when the preferences directory isn't writable, or from a source
checkout of the e2e repository.

## See what would be sent

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1 npx e2e run
```

```bash pnpm
E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1 pnpm exec e2e run
```

```bash bun
E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1 bunx e2e run
```
</CodeGroup>

The CLI prints the exact payloads to stderr as `[telemetry] {...}` and
sends nothing.

## What is sent

Each command sends one `e2e_cli_session` event. `run` and `explore` also
send `e2e_run_completed`, `init` sends `e2e_init_completed`, `upgrade` sends
`e2e_upgrade_completed`, and `mcp` sends one `e2e_mcp_session` per MCP
session. `--help` and `--version` send
nothing, on any command. `run()` from `e2e/runner` sends no session event,
only one `e2e_run_completed` per run that returns a report.

The events go in one request when the command or `run()` ends, with a
two-second deadline. `e2e mcp` sends each session event in its own request,
and `e2e run --watch` sends each run's event when that run ends.

Events hold only the properties below. An error code that isn't an upper-case
token is sent as `OTHER`. An engine, platform, model, fleet, or MCP client
name, or an MCP client version, that isn't a plain token of letters, digits,
dots, dashes, and underscores is sent as `other`. An engine version that isn't
semver is sent as `unversioned`. In action and tool call counts, a project's
own tools count together as `tool`, and any other name as `other`.

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Every event">

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `distinct_id` | A random id stored in the preferences file. CI uses `ci:<vendor>` instead, and a fleet uses `fleet:<name>` (see [In a fleet](#in-a-fleet)) |
| `project_id` | A hash of the repository's root commit, shared across full clones. `null` outside git and in a shallow clone |
| `session_id` | A random id for this one invocation |
| `first_run`, `days_since_first_run` | Whether this command created the preferences file, and whole days since then. `null` in CI, in a fleet, and for a preferences file from before the time was recorded |
| `os`, `os_release`, `arch`, `cpu_count`, `memory_gb`, `docker`, `wsl`, `tty` | The machine class |
| `sandbox` | The microVM the kernel announces itself as (`firecracker`), else `null` |
| `ci`, `ci_name` | Whether `CI` is set, and the vendor when one announces itself (`github-actions`, `gitlab`, `circleci`, ...) |
| `fleet` | The value of `E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET`, `null` when unset |
| `coding_agent` | The coding agent whose shell ran the command, when one announces itself (`claude-code`, `cursor`, `codex`, ...) |
| `e2e_version`, `package_manager` | The e2e version, and the package manager that started the CLI |
| `runtime`, `runtime_version`, `node_version` | `node`, `bun`, or `deno`, and its version. `node_version` is Node's own version, or the Node compatibility version under Bun or Deno |
| `$lib`, `$lib_version`, `$process_person_profile`, `$geoip_disable` | `e2e`, its version, `false`, and `true`: PostHog keeps no person profile and derives no location |

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="e2e_cli_session, once per command">

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `command` | `init`, `run`, `list`, `cache ls`, `guide`, `telemetry`, ... |
| `flags` | The names of the flags given, such as `--headed` or `--tag`. Never their values |
| `exit_code`, `duration_ms` | How the command ended and how long it took |
| `error_code` | The runner code of the failure that stopped the command before it could run (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_CONFIG`, ...), `CLI_USAGE` for a flag or argument the CLI rejected, else `null` |

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="e2e_init_completed, once per e2e init">

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | `scaffolded`, `already-initialized`, `cancelled`, `install-failed`, `not-interactive`, `invalid-project`, or `example-failed` |
| `yes`, `existing_config` | Whether `--yes` was given, and whether a config already existed, so no engine or gateway was asked |
| `example` | The `--example` name (`with-vite`, `with-expo`, ...), `null` without the flag |
| `engine`, `gateway` | The ids of the engine and the model gateway chosen for a new config (`web`, `mobile`, `none`; `vercel`, `openrouter`, `openai-compatible`, `chatgpt`, `copilot`, `opencode-console`, `grok`, `none`), `null` when not asked. Never the endpoint typed for an OpenAI-compatible gateway |
| `skill`, `mcp`, `install` | Whether the agent skill, the MCP registration, and the dependency install were chosen |

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="e2e_upgrade_completed, once per e2e upgrade">

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | `upgraded`, `up-to-date`, `dry-run`, `no-project`, `invalid-project`, `linked`, `unknown-target`, `incompatible`, `registry-failed`, or `install-failed` |
| `target` | `version` for a named version, else the dist-tag: `latest`, `nightly`, `canary`, `beta`, or `other` |
| `from_version`, `to_version`, `prerelease` | The `e2e` version installed before, the one the target resolved to, and whether that one is a prerelease. `null` when unknown |
| `manager` | The package manager the command picked for the project: `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, or `bun`. It installs only on `upgraded`. `null` when the command stopped before picking one |
| `siblings` | The `@e2e-dev` packages in the upgrade plan, without the scope: `["web", "kernel"]`. Linked packages and ones the registry doesn't have are left out |
| `packages_moved`, `packages_linked` | How many `e2e` and `@e2e-dev` entries in `package.json` the upgrade rewrote, and how many it left alone because they aren't registry versions (`workspace:`, `file:`, `catalog:`, a path, git, an alias). Not the lockfile's package count |

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="e2e_run_completed, once per e2e run, e2e explore, or completed run()">

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `command` | `run`, `explore`, or `runner.run` for `run()` from `e2e/runner` |
| `status`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms` | The run's outcome |
| `flags` | The names of the flags given to the run command, never their values |
| `tests_discovered`, `tests_selected`, `tests_executed`, `tests_passed`, `tests_failed`, `tests_interrupted`, `tests_flaky`, `tests_skipped` | The summary counts |
| `attempts_total`, `tests_retried` | How many attempts the run made across tests and serial groups, and how many of these needed more than one |
| `filters_run`, `filters_timed_out`, `filters_failed`, `filters_skipped`, `filters_changed_files`, `tests_left_out_by_filters` | How many [test filters](/filters) the run applied, how many ran out of time, and how many failed, whether a run with `--changed-since` called none of them, such as when no file changed, how many files the change had, and how many tests the filters left out. Never a filter's name, reason, or note, a path, or a commit |
| `targets`, `platforms`, `engines` | How many targets, on which platforms, and with which engines and versions: `web`, `ios`, `web@0.6.1`, or your own engine's name and version |
| `steps_total`, `steps_agent`, `steps_locator`, `steps_assertion`, `steps_screen`, `steps_app`, `steps_session`, `steps_resource` | Step counts by kind |
| `steps_agent_act`, `steps_agent_assert`, `steps_agent_extract`, `steps_agent_waitfor` | The agent steps by entry point |
| `tests_with_agent_steps`, `tests_with_act` | How many executed tests ran any agent step, and how many ran `agent.act` |
| `agent_steps_replayed`, `agent_steps_partial`, `agent_steps_missed`, `agent_steps_uncached`, `agent_steps_vision` | How the replay cache served the agent steps, how many `agent.act` steps ran with the cache off, and how many used pixel evidence |
| `agent_miss_reasons`, `agent_handoff_reasons` | Why steps missed the cache and why replays handed off to the agent, by the runner's own reason names: `{"no-entry": 3, "retry": 1}` |
| `tests_code_only`, `tests_replayed`, `tests_assisted`, `tests_live` | The executed tests by how the cache carried them: no agent step, every agent step replayed from the cache, the agent ran but the cache carried part of a step, the agent ran every agent step |
| `agent_actions` | How often the agent took each action, by the runner's own names: `{"tap": 12, "typeText": 3, "scroll": 2}` |
| `model_gateway`, `model_provider`, `model_id`, `model_calls`, `model_tokens`, `model_cached_tokens`, `estimated_cost_usd` | For the first model-backed step: the AI SDK provider that served it (`gateway` for the Vercel AI Gateway, `openrouter.chat`, `openai.chat`, ...), the vendor (the first segment of a `vendor/model` id, else the provider), and the public model id. Then the run's totals |
| `model_calls_act`, `model_calls_assert`, `model_calls_extract`, `model_calls_waitfor` | The model calls by agent entry point |
| `cost_source` | `provider` when the provider priced the calls, `none` when nobody priced them, `null` for a run without model calls |
| `artifact_bytes` | The size of the artifacts the run wrote |
| `errors`, `error_codes` | How many run-level errors, and the distinct error codes seen anywhere in the run (`LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, `APP_UNREACHABLE`, ...), at most 20 |
| `primary_error_code` | The first error the run recorded, which decided its status: a run-level error, else the failed attempt's verdict, else a step's. `null` for a clean run |
| `error_kinds` | For `ENGINE_FAILURE`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, and `ERROR`: the code and a kind read off the message against a closed list (`auth`, `rate-limit`, `overloaded`, `timeout`, `network`, `server`, `bad-request`, `device`, `daemon`, `browser`, `permission`, `not-found`, `memory`, `other`), as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED:rate-limit`. Only the kind's name leaves the machine, never the message |

Config features, absent when the config didn't load. Each is a count, a
boolean, or one of the runner's own option values, never text you wrote:

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `config_workers`, `config_retries` | The worker count and retries the run resolved |
| `config_agents`, `config_custom_executor`, `config_separate_judge`, `config_project_tools` | How many agents are configured, whether any has a custom executor or a judge model of its own, and how many distinct project tools they declare |
| `config_credentials`, `config_secrets` | How many credentials and secrets are configured |
| `config_cache_mode`, `config_cache_store`, `config_cache_strict` | `off`, `read-only`, or `read-write`; `file` or `custom`; whether strict replay is on |
| `config_reporters`, `config_custom_reporters`, `config_artifact_store` | The built-in reporter ids (`list`, `json`, `junit`, `markdown`), how many reporter objects the config adds, and whether an artifact store is set |
| `config_filters` | How many test filters the config declares |
| `config_trace_modes`, `config_video_modes` | The distinct recording modes across targets (`off`, `on`, `retain-on-failure`, `on-first-retry`, `on-all-retries`) |
| `config_app_commands`, `config_environments` | How many targets start an app command, and the distinct app environments (`test`, `staging`, `production`) |

On `e2e explore` only, counts of what the exploration was given and found:

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `explore_ended` | Why it stopped: `finished`, `step-limit`, `time`, `stuck`, or `aborted` |
| `explore_max_steps`, `explore_timeout_ms` | The budgets it ran with |
| `explore_steps`, `explore_steps_passed`, `explore_steps_failed`, `explore_steps_blocked`, `explore_steps_exhausted` | Exploration steps, by how each ended |
| `explore_assessed` | Whether the agent gave a closing assessment |
| `explore_issues`, `explore_warnings`, `explore_findings_by_severity` | Findings by kind, and by severity: `{"1": 0, "2": 1, "3": 0, "4": 0, "5": 1}` |

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="e2e_mcp_session, once per MCP session">

An `e2e mcp` server sends one for each `open_session` it receives, when the
session closes or the open fails. A session that is still open when the
client kills the server isn't sent.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `client`, `client_version` | The name and version the MCP client gives itself (`claude-code`, `cursor-vscode`, ...). `null` before the client introduced itself |
| `outcome`, `error_code` | `closed` for a session that opened, `open-failed` with the runner code of the failure (`APP_UNREACHABLE`, `ENGINE_FAILURE`, ...) |
| `ended_by` | `agent` for `close_session`, `idle`, `step` for the session's time limit, `server` when the server shut down. `null` for a failed open |
| `platform`, `engine`, `headed` | The target's platform and engine with its version, as for a run, and whether the UI was shown |
| `duration_ms`, `sessions_open` | How long the session lived, and how many other sessions were open when it opened |
| `calls_total`, `calls_failed`, `calls` | Tool calls, failed calls, and calls by the session's own tool names: `{"observe": 4, "tap": 9, "locate": 2, "screenshot": 1}` |
| `error_codes` | How often each runner code failed a call: `{"LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND": 2}`, at most 20 codes |

</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## What is never sent

Telemetry never sends test titles, file paths, URLs, origins, instructions,
observations, page content, screenshots, error messages, stack traces,
environment variable values, credentials, or file contents. It never sends
the names of targets, agents, credentials, secrets, or project tools, MCP
tool arguments or results, an exploration's goal or charters, or its
findings' words.

## In CI

CI runs count as the CI vendor, not as a machine, with no preferences file
and no notice. A coding agent that sets `CI` in its shell, with no CI vendor
around it, counts as the machine it runs on.

In CI, only the environment variables turn telemetry off. Set
`E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'` in the job's `env`.

## In a fleet

A platform that runs e2e for its users on new machines would count each
machine as a new user. Set `E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET=<name>` on those machines.
Their events count as `fleet:<name>`, with no preferences file and no
notice, as in CI. Or set `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` to send nothing.

## Where it goes

Events go to `eu.i.posthog.com`, a PostHog project that the e2e
maintainers operate. PostHog keeps no person profile, stores no request
address, and skips GeoIP for each event. The data is read in aggregate.

Telemetry falls under the
[security policy](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
[Outbound connections](/reference/security#outbound-connections) lists every
other connection a run can make.

## Feedback

[`e2e feedback`](/reference/cli#e2e-feedback) isn't telemetry. It sends the
words in its flags as one `e2e_feedback` event to the same PostHog project,
with the machine facts above. When telemetry is on, it has the same anonymous
id as your telemetry events.

A saved `e2e telemetry disable` doesn't stop it. `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`
and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` do. The [CLI reference](/reference/cli#e2e-feedback)
covers redaction, `--dry-run`, and bugs without `--repro`.

## The notice

The first command, or the first `run()` from `e2e/runner`, prints a notice
on stderr that tells how to opt out. It leaves `--reporter json` output
intact. `e2e init` and `e2e telemetry` don't print it, so it waits for the
next command. The notice shows again after a large change to the data
collected.

---
title: Security
description: What the model can see and do, how secrets stay out of it, and what you still need to watch.
icon: "shield-halved"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/security.png?v=6c43d95c56"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/security.png?v=6c43d95c56"
---

e2e trusts the code you write and treats everything the app shows as
untrusted. App content can't grant the model tools, credentials, or a
larger budget.

## How secrets stay out of the model

A `Secret` is a handle with no plaintext accessor. The model sees only its
name and purpose. When the model asks to fill one, the runner checks the
field and types the value itself.

After a secret fill, the model gets no screenshots for the rest of the
attempt, because the app could show the value anywhere. Every known secret value becomes
`<secret:name>` in model input, reports, console output, and `.txt`,
`.csv`, `.json`, `.html`, and `.htm` downloads.

## What can still leak

Redaction matches strings, and only a secret fill turns model screenshots off:

- **Screenshots, video, and downloads.** Screenshots mask secure fields
  only, video masks nothing, and a download other than a redacted text file
  is kept as served. If the test typed a password, check them before you
  share them.
- **`command.log`.** It holds your app's stdout and stderr verbatim. Keep
  secrets out of your app's output.
- **Transformed values.** The last four characters of a key, or its base64,
  pass through. Assert the outcome, not the secret.
- **Values not filled as a secret.** A secret passed as a plain string, or a
  sign-in that sets a cookie, leaves model screenshots on. Only a configured
  secret's value is redacted.
- **Request credentials.** `basicAuth` answers a `401` from any origin.
  `headers` reach every host under a shared domain such as `vercel.app`.
- **Committed recordings.** Cache entries store typed values verbatim, except
  secret fills. They aren't signed and replay with your permissions, so
  review them as you would test code.

[Where redaction stops](/reference/security#where-redaction-stops) lists
every case.

## What the model sees and does

The model sees your instruction, the screen as an accessibility tree, the
redacted URL, and records of earlier steps in the test. It gets a masked
screenshot when it asks for one or a step sets `vision`.

The model acts only through tools. The runner checks each call against a
closed schema before it runs, and never evaluates model text as code. A call
that breaks a rule, such as a navigation to `file:`, fails with
`POLICY_DENIED`. There is no origin allowlist: the agent can follow the app
to another site and use the step's secrets there.

## What runs with your permissions

Your tests, config, engines, tools, reporters, stores, secret providers, and
app commands run with your operating-system permissions, unsandboxed. Run
untrusted pull request code in an external sandbox with no secrets or write
tokens.

## What leaves your computer

A run connects to your model provider, the app under test, and, unless you
opt out, [telemetry](/telemetry) at `eu.i.posthog.com`. There is no crash
reporting. A CLI command on a terminal checks `registry.npmjs.org` for a
newer release at most once a day, `e2e feedback` checks before each
report unless `--allow-outdated`, and `e2e upgrade` reads the versions of
the e2e packages the project lists. Integrations such as Kernel, EAS Simulators, Limrun, and smol add
their own destinations, listed with the rest under
[Outbound connections](/reference/security#outbound-connections).

## Report a vulnerability

Report privately through
[GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/security/advisories/new)
or by mail to security@tester.army. The
[security policy](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
states response times and supported versions.
