`expect(locator)` waits for an app condition, `expect(screen)` compares the
screen against a stored screenshot, and `expect(value)` checks a value
immediately. `expect.poll` re-reads a value until its matcher passes,
`expect.soft` keeps a failure for the end of the test body instead of
throwing it, and `expect.any` and the other
[asymmetric matchers](#asymmetric-matchers) stand in for values inside a
structural comparison.

```ts title="tests/checkout.e2e.ts"
import { expect, test } from 'e2e';

test('checkout summary', async ({ screen }) => {
  await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Checkout')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(screen.getByTestId('line-item')).toHaveCount(2);
  const total = await screen.getByTestId('total').textContent();
  expect(total).toContain('$');
});
```

## Reference

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| [`expect(locator)`](#locator-matchers) | `AsyncExpectation` |
| [`expect(screen)`](#screenshot-matchers) | `ScreenExpectation` |
| [`expect(fixture)`](#browser-matchers) | The engine's matcher set |
| [`expect(value, message?)`](#value-matchers) | `ValueExpectation<T>` |
| [`expect.poll(read, options?)`](#polling-a-value) | `PollExpectation<T>` |
| [`expect.soft(actual)`](#soft-assertions) | The same matchers, failures kept |
| [`expect.any(Class)` and others](#asymmetric-matchers) | `AsymmetricMatcher` |

`expect` tells the argument apart by what it is:

- Engine fixtures can provide matchers, such as `expect(browser).toHaveURL()`.
  Such a fixture is an `Expectable<E>`: its engine attached the matcher set
  `E` through [`expectable`](/reference/engine#contributed-fixtures), and
  `expect(fixture)` returns it.
- Every other argument gets the value matchers, a promise included. Await a
  promise before passing its result to `expect`.

The declarations are under [Types](#types).

### Locator matchers

`expect(locator)` returns an `AsyncExpectation`. Each matcher polls until it
holds or its timeout passes, under the rules in [Behavior](#behavior):
[Strictness](#strictness), [Text matching](#text-matching), and
[Secure fields](#secure-fields) among them. The options are in
[`AsyncExpectation`](#asyncexpectation-and-textmatcheroptions).

| Matcher | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`toBeVisible`](#tobevisible-and-tobehidden) | Waits for visibility |
| [`toBeHidden`](#tobevisible-and-tobehidden) | Waits for hidden or absent state |
| [`toBeAttached`](#tobeattached) | Waits for one match to exist |
| [`toBeEnabled`](#tobeenabled-and-tobedisabled) | Waits for enabled state |
| [`toBeDisabled`](#tobeenabled-and-tobedisabled) | Waits for disabled state |
| [`toBeChecked`](#tobechecked-tobeselected-and-tobeexpanded) | Waits for checked state |
| [`toBeSelected`](#tobechecked-tobeselected-and-tobeexpanded) | Waits for selected state |
| [`toBeExpanded`](#tobechecked-tobeselected-and-tobeexpanded) | Waits for expanded state |
| [`toBeFocused`](#tobefocused) | Waits for focused state |
| [`toHaveText`](#tohavetext-and-tocontaintext) | Waits for exact normalized text |
| [`toContainText`](#tohavetext-and-tocontaintext) | Waits for contained normalized text |
| [`toHaveValue`](#tohavevalue) | Waits for a form control's value |
| [`toHaveAttribute`](#tohaveattribute) | Waits for an attribute |
| [`toHaveCount`](#tohavecount) | Waits for an exact match count |
| [`toHaveAccessibleName`](#tohaveaccessiblename) | Waits for an accessible name |
| [`toHaveScreenshot`](#screenshot-matchers) | Compares with a stored screenshot |

#### `toBeVisible` and `toBeHidden`

`toBeVisible` waits for the one match to be shown. `toBeHidden` waits for a
hidden or absent state.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();
await expect(screen.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });
await expect(screen.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible({ visible: false }); // as toBeHidden()
```

#### `toBeAttached`

Waits for one match to exist, hidden or shown, where `toBeVisible` needs a
shown one.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByText('Loaded')).toBeAttached();
await expect(screen.getByText('Loading')).toBeAttached({ attached: false });
```

Negated, or with `attached: false`, it waits for no match and passes once
nothing matches.

#### `toBeEnabled` and `toBeDisabled`

`toBeEnabled` waits for an enabled node; `toBeDisabled` waits for a disabled
one.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('button', 'Pay')).toBeEnabled();
await expect(screen.getByRole('button', 'Pay')).toBeEnabled({ enabled: false }); // as toBeDisabled()
```

A node is enabled unless it reports `disabled`. On the web, `disabled` is
the state the browser applies, not the attribute alone. That is the reading
Playwright's `toBeDisabled` gives:

- A control inside a `<fieldset disabled>` is disabled unless it sits in
  that fieldset's first `<legend>`.
- `aria-disabled="true"` on an ancestor disables the widgets below it until
  an `aria-disabled="false"` cuts the chain.

#### `toBeChecked`, `toBeSelected`, and `toBeExpanded`

Each waits for its state: checked, selected, or expanded.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Subscribe')).toBeChecked({ checked: false });
await expect(screen.getByRole('tab', 'Billing')).toBeSelected();
```

A missing `checked`, `selected`, or `expanded` state counts as `false`, so
`.not.toBeChecked()` passes on a button or a heading.

#### `toBeFocused`

Waits for focused state.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Email')).toBeFocused();
```

#### `toHaveText` and `toContainText`

`toHaveText` waits for exact normalized text; `toContainText` waits for
contained normalized text. Both take a single `TextMatch` or a list.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Saved');
await expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).not.toContainText('error', { ignoreCase: true });
await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toHaveText(['Write spec', /^Ship/, 'Release']);
await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toContainText(['spec', 'runner', 'Release']);
await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toContainText(['spec', 'Release']);
```

A list form's failure message lists every text observed.

| Form | Holds when |
| --- | --- |
| `toHaveText([...])` | The match count equals the list length, and the match at each position satisfies the entry there: a string exactly after normalization, a `RegExp` by test. An empty list holds when nothing matches |
| `toContainText([...])` | Each entry is contained by a distinct match, in list order, as Playwright's does. Extra matches before, between, or after are fine, a repeated entry needs a match of its own, and an empty list always holds |

<Note>
Negated, `toContainText([...])` fails as soon as that ordered subsequence
exists, so `not.toContainText(['Deleted'])` fails while any match contains
`Deleted`.
</Note>

#### `toHaveValue`

Waits for a form control's value, compared as it is.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Email')).toHaveValue('ada@example.test');
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Search')).toHaveValue('');
```

- No normalization: newlines and trailing spaces count, and the failure
  message prints the value that way.
- A `contenteditable` editor's value is its rendered text, kept the same way.
  An empty editor reads as `''`.
- A control the platform reports without a value, such as a cleared field on
  a device, reads as `''`.
- A node whose role carries no value, such as a heading or a link, never
  satisfies `toHaveValue`, negated or not. The message reads
  `no value (not a form control)`.

#### `toHaveAttribute`

Waits for the attribute to be present; with `value`, for it to match.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('link', 'Help')).toHaveAttribute('target');
await expect(screen.getByRole('link', 'Help')).toHaveAttribute('href', '/help');
```

#### `toHaveCount`

Waits for an exact match count.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toHaveCount(3);
```

#### `toHaveAccessibleName`

Waits for an accessible name.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i })).toHaveAccessibleName('Close');
```

### Screenshot matchers

`expect(screen)` and `expect(locator)` compare against a PNG stored beside
the test file, on every engine that captures pixels. The
[Visual comparison](/visual-testing) guide shows the workflow.

| Matcher | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot`](#tohavescreenshot) | Compares the whole screen |
| [`expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot`](#tohavescreenshot) | Compares a locator's one match |

#### `toHaveScreenshot`

Waits for the screen, or the one match of a locator, to look like its stored
screenshot: `name`, or one named after the test.

```ts
await expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot('home.png');
await expect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toHaveScreenshot();
await expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot('feed.png', { mask: [screen.getByTestId('timestamp')], maxDiffPixels: 50 });
```

Both forms take the [Screenshot options](#screenshot-options).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Stored at | `<test file>-snapshots/<name>-<target>-<os>.png`; `.png` is added to a name without it |
| Unnamed | The test's title path, lowercase, and a count: `checkout-pays-by-card-1` |
| Missing | Taken from two screenshots in a row that are the same within the tolerance, then `ASSERTION_FAILED`. Written beside the test; in CI without `--update-snapshots` only attached to the results, at `snapshots/<path in the project>` |
| Written earlier in the run | Without `--update-snapshots`, and always for `.not`, no comparison passes against a screenshot the same run wrote (a retry, a repeat, another test naming it): `ASSERTION_FAILED` until the next run. With `--update-snapshots` a positive matcher compares and may write it again |
| Different | Retried until one matches or the timeout; then `ASSERTION_FAILED` with `-expected`, `-actual`, and `-diff` images on the step |
| `--update-snapshots`, `-u` | A missing or different stored screenshot is written from a screen that holds still, and the matcher passes |
| `.not` | Passes once the screen differs; with nothing stored it is `ASSERTION_FAILED` |
| Tolerance | Both `maxDiffPixels` and `maxDiffPixelRatio` set: the smaller wins |

| Throws | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | Before the screen is read: a name with a path separator, an option the matcher does not take (Playwright's `fullPage`, `animations`, `clip`), a value out of range, or `expect` on a screen scoped to a frame. Compare a locator inside the frame instead |
| `ASSERTION_FAILED` | A missing, different, or same-run stored screenshot, as in the table above |
| `POLICY_DENIED` | The engine can't prove every secure field on screen is masked |

#### Screenshot options

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold` | `number` | `0.2` |
| `maxDiffPixels` | `number` | `0` |
| `maxDiffPixelRatio` | `number` | `0` |
| `mask` | `readonly Locator[]` | - |
| `maskColor` | `string` | `#ff00ff` |
| `timeout` | `number` | `config.assertionTimeout` |

[`ScreenshotOptions`](#screenexpectation-and-screenshotoptions) describes
each option.

### browser matchers

Contributed by `@e2e-dev/web`; the `BrowserExpectation` type is exported
from that package. Every matcher call is a recorded `expect.<matcher>`
assertion step.

| Matcher | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`toHaveURL`](#tohaveurl) | Waits for the current URL |
| [`toHaveTitle`](#tohavetitle) | Waits for the current title |
| [`toHaveClass`](#tohaveclass) | Waits for a target's `class` |

Any other option key is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, such as `ignoreCase` on
`toHaveTitle`, which Playwright does not take either.

#### `toHaveURL`

Waits for the current URL to match.

```ts
await expect(browser).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
await expect(browser).toHaveURL(/\/orders\/\d+$/);
```

- A relative string resolves against the base URL and matches exactly after
  normalization.
- A `RegExp` tests the full URL.
- Anything else, such as a predicate function, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- It takes Playwright's `ignoreCase`, as the locator matchers do
  ([Text matching](#text-matching)).

#### `toHaveTitle`

Waits for the current title to match.

```ts
await expect(browser).toHaveTitle(/Dashboard/);
```

#### `toHaveClass`

Waits for the target's `class` attribute to match: a string is the whole
normalized class list, a `RegExp` is tested against it.

```ts
await expect(browser).toHaveClass(browser.locator('.card'), 'card active');
```

- It polls for the node too: a target that matches nothing yet is one more
  poll, not a failure, until the assertion timeout runs out.
- An ambiguous target still fails at once with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`.
- It reads the `class` attribute, so `''` matches `class=""` and not an
  element with no `class` attribute at all. Playwright's `toHaveClass('')`
  accepts both.

### Value matchers

`expect(value)` runs synchronously without retrying. For a value that may
still change, use [Polling a value](#polling-a-value).

| Matcher | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`toBe`](#tobe) | Compares with `Object.is` |
| [`toEqual`](#toequal) | Recursive structural equality |
| [`toMatchObject`](#tomatchobject) | Recursive subset match |
| [`toBeTruthy`, `toBeFalsy`](#tobetruthy-and-tobefalsy) | Truthy or falsy value |
| [`toBeNull`, `toBeUndefined`, `toBeDefined`](#tobenull-tobeundefined-and-tobedefined) | `null`, `undefined`, or defined |
| [`toHaveLength`](#tohavelength) | `length` equals `expected` |
| [`toHaveProperty`](#tohaveproperty) | Property at a path |
| [`toContain`](#tocontain) | String or collection containment |
| [`toMatch`](#tomatch) | String or `RegExp` match |
| [`toBeGreaterThan` and others](#numeric-comparisons) | Numeric bound holds |
| [`toBeCloseTo`](#tobecloseto) | Within `10 ** -digits / 2` |
| [`toMatchSchema`](#matching-a-schema) | Standard Schema validation |

A matcher that cannot evaluate its value fails as `ASSERTION_FAILED`, like a
mismatch. Examples are `toContain` on a number, or `toHaveLength` on a value
without a numeric `length`. So under `expect.poll`, a value that has not
taken its final shape yet is one more failing sample.

#### `toBe`

Compares with `Object.is`.

```ts
expect(status).toBe('paid');
```

#### `toEqual`

Performs recursive structural equality the way Jest's does.

```ts
expect(payload).toEqual({ ok: true, items: [{ sku: 'a' }] });
```

- Primitives compare with `Object.is`, so `NaN` equals `NaN` and `0` does not
  equal `-0`.
- Arrays and plain objects compare by their contents, `Date` by time,
  `RegExp` by source and flags, `Map` and `Set` by their entries.
- A property whose value is `undefined` is treated as absent, and a sparse
  array equals one holding `undefined`.
- Class types are not compared: a class instance equals a plain object with
  the same properties. There is no `toStrictEqual`; see
  [Not included](#not-included).

#### `toMatchObject`

Requires every property of `expected` to match recursively.

```ts
expect(order).toMatchObject({ customer: { name: 'Ada' }, lines: [{ sku: 'a' }, { sku: 'b' }] });
```

- Properties `expected` does not name are ignored.
- An array in `expected` matches an array of the same length, element by
  element, each element again as a subset.
- Both sides must be objects; a primitive on either side is refused.

#### `toBeTruthy` and `toBeFalsy`

Require a truthy or a falsy value.

```ts
expect(created).toBeTruthy();
```

#### `toBeNull`, `toBeUndefined`, and `toBeDefined`

`toBeNull` requires `null` and `toBeUndefined` requires `undefined`.
`toBeDefined` requires any value but `undefined`; `null` passes.

```ts
expect(row).toBeDefined();
```

#### `toHaveLength`

Requires a `length` property equal to `expected`: a string, an array, or
anything array-like.

```ts
expect(items).toHaveLength(3);
```

#### `toHaveProperty`

Requires the property at `path` to exist; with `expected`, to equal it by
`toEqual` rules.

```ts
expect(order).toHaveProperty('customer.email', 'ada@example.test');
expect(order).toHaveProperty(['lines', 0, 'sku'], 'a');
```

- `path` is dotted (`'user.address.city'`) or an array of keys
  (`['user', 'address', 'city']`). Use the array form when a key contains a
  dot, or to index an array by number.
- Inherited properties count, and a property holding `undefined` exists.
- A string, number, or boolean on the path is read through its wrapper
  object, as in Jest, so `toHaveProperty('label.length', 3)` and
  `toHaveProperty(['label', 0], 'a')` reach into a string.
- `null` and `undefined` have no properties.

#### `toContain`

Requires string or collection containment.

```ts
expect(total).toContain('$');
expect(rows).toContain(expect.objectContaining({ status: 'paid' }));
```

- On a string, `expected` must be a string, and it is a substring check. An
  asymmetric matcher is refused there:
  `expect('abc').toContain(expect.stringContaining('a'))` fails.
- On a collection, an element must equal `expected`. This form takes
  [asymmetric matchers](#asymmetric-matchers).

#### `toMatch`

Requires a string or `RegExp` match.

```ts
expect(id).toMatch(/^usr_/);
```

A pattern that is neither a string nor a `RegExp` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

#### Numeric comparisons

`toBeGreaterThan` and `toBeLessThan` require a numeric bound;
`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` and `toBeLessThanOrEqual` require it inclusive.

```ts
expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(1);
expect(count).toBeLessThanOrEqual(10);
```

#### `toBeCloseTo`

Requires a number within `10 ** -digits / 2` of `expected`.

```ts
expect(totals.lineTotal).toBeCloseTo(60); // digits default: 2
```

`toBeCloseTo(60)` accepts 59.996 and rejects 59.99. Infinite values pass only
when they are the same infinity.

#### Matching a schema

`toMatchSchema` validates a value against a
[Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev): a Zod, Valibot, or ArkType
schema, or any library that implements the spec. Pass the schema your app
already parses its API with, and the test fails when the API drifts from it.
It returns the schema's output, typed, so the rest of the test reads
properties without casting.

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

const User = z.object({ id: z.number(), name: z.string(), email: z.email() });

const users = expect(await response.json()).toMatchSchema(z.array(User));
expect(users.map((user) => user.name)).toContain('Ada');
```

- A failure lists every issue by its path (`1.email: Invalid email address`).
- The output is the schema's, so defaults and transforms apply.
- A matcher returns before anything could await it, so a schema that
  validates asynchronously (an async refinement) is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- Negated, it passes when the value does not match and returns nothing.

#### Failure messages

Pass a second argument to describe the check in its failure message:

```ts
expect(created, 'the company exists through the API').toBeTruthy();
// ASSERTION_FAILED: the company exists through the API: expected undefined to be truthy
```

Only value expectations take a message; a locator or `browser` expectation
already names its locator and matcher in the failure.

#### Not included

The unit-runner matchers (`toThrow`, `toBeInstanceOf`, `toBeNaN`,
`toStrictEqual`, `resolves`, `rejects`, `expect.extend`) are not part of
`expect`. An end-to-end test checks what the app shows and what its API
returns; the value matchers cover that, see [API](/api-testing). Code-level
checks belong in the unit runner.

### Asymmetric matchers

An asymmetric matcher stands in for a value inside `toEqual`,
`toMatchObject`, the collection form of `toContain`, and the value of
`toHaveProperty`. Where the comparison would test equality, it asks the
matcher instead. They are Jest's matchers, with Jest's rules.

| Matcher | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `expect.any(Class)` | An instance of the class. For `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `BigInt`, `Symbol`, and `Function`, the primitive too; for `Object`, anything `typeof` calls an object, `null` included |
| `expect.anything()` | Anything but `null` and `undefined` |
| `expect.objectContaining(sample)` | An object whose properties include every property of `sample`, each compared by `toEqual` rules |
| `expect.arrayContaining(sample)` | An array holding every element of `sample`, in any order, each compared by `toEqual` rules |
| `expect.stringContaining(text)` | A string with `text` as a substring |
| `expect.stringMatching(text \| RegExp)` | A string the RegExp tests true on; a text sample is compiled to a RegExp, so `'a.b'` matches `'axb'` |

```ts
expect(created).toEqual({
  id: expect.stringMatching(/^usr_/),
  createdAt: expect.any(String),
  roles: expect.arrayContaining(['member']),
  profile: expect.objectContaining({ name: 'Ada' }),
});
expect(rows).toContain(expect.objectContaining({ status: 'paid' }));
expect(response).toHaveProperty('body.total', expect.any(Number));
```

- In a failure message a matcher prints as its description: `Any<Number>`,
  `ObjectContaining {"name":"Ada"}`.
- Matchers nest: an `objectContaining` sample may hold an `expect.any`.
- The string form of `toContain` refuses them; see [`toContain`](#tocontain).

### Soft assertions

`expect.soft(actual)` takes what `expect(actual)` takes and returns the same
matchers. A soft matcher that fails does not throw: the failure is kept on
the running attempt and the body continues.

```ts
test('checkout summary', async ({ agent, screen }) => {
  await agent.act('add the "Pro" plan to the cart and open the summary');
  expect.soft(await screen.getByTestId('subtotal').textContent()).toBe('$40.00');
  expect.soft(await screen.getByTestId('tax').textContent()).toBe('$8.00');
  await expect.soft(screen.getByRole('button', 'Pay')).toBeEnabled();
  await expect(screen.getByTestId('total')).toHaveText('$48.00');
});
```

```text
ASSERTION_FAILED: 2 soft assertions failed
1. expected "$41.00" to be "$40.00"
2. expect.toBeEnabled failed
   locator: getByRole('button', 'Pay')
   expected: enabled
   observed: states: disabled (match count 1)
```

- Once the body has settled, and before `afterEach`, the attempt fails with
  one `ASSERTION_FAILED` that lists every kept failure in order. The error's
  source line is the first soft matcher that failed.
- A soft locator or `browser` matcher is still a recorded `expect.<matcher>`
  step, marked failed, so the report shows where in the flow it landed.
- A soft value matcher is not a step, the same as a hard one; its failure
  appears in the attempt's error records.
- When the body throws on its own, or times out, that error stays the
  attempt's verdict and the soft failures are recorded beside it under
  `secondaryErrors`.
- A body that skips itself with `test.skip(...)` after a soft failure still
  fails: the soft failures are the attempt's error, and the skip reason is
  kept in the attempt's `skip`.
- A soft `toMatchSchema` returns the schema's output when the value matches
  and `undefined` after a kept failure, and its type says so.

<Note>
Outside a test body there is nothing to keep a failure for, so `expect.soft`
throws at once like `expect`: in a standalone script, and in an `afterEach`
hook, which runs after the soft failures have been settled. There is no
`expect.soft.poll`; `expect.poll` has its own timeout to fail on.
</Note>

### Polling a value

`expect.poll(read)` re-reads a value until a matcher passes. Use it to wait
for an API response or saved data after an app action.

```ts
await agent.act('create a test named "AI checkout regression" described as {description}', {
  params: { description },
});
await expect
  .poll(() => getTest(workspace).then((row) => row?.title), { timeout: 15_000 })
  .toBe('AI checkout regression');
await expect.poll(async () => (await listTests(workspace)).length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
await expect.poll(() => readStatus(), { message: 'the batch never finished' }).not.toBe('running');
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | `number` | `config.assertionTimeout` during an attempt, 5000 ms outside one |
| `interval` | `number` | `100` |
| `message` | `string` | - |

- `timeout` is the deadline in milliseconds, a finite number 0 or more. It is
  capped by the test deadline in the body, or the hook's `cleanupTimeout`
  during `afterEach`.
- `interval` is the pause between reads in milliseconds, a finite number
  above 0.
- `message` is an extra line in the timeout error, after the matcher line.

Every value matcher is available, returning a promise.

- Each sample calls `read` and runs the matcher. A matcher failure or a
  `read` that throws is one failing sample; a `read` that hangs is cut at the
  deadline.
- `toMatchSchema` resolves to the schema's output for the passing read.
- When the attempt is cancelled, the loop stops with `CANCELLED`. At the
  attempt's deadline it stops with `ASSERTION_FAILED`, naming the deadline.
  A `read` in flight is abandoned, not stopped: work it started can go on.
- `expect.poll` is not recorded as a report step; a timeout surfaces only as
  the test's failure.

At the deadline it throws `ASSERTION_FAILED` naming the matcher, then
`message` when given, then the last sample: the last matcher failure, the
last `read` error, or `no read completed`.

```text
expect.poll(...).not.toBe(...) timed out after 5000 ms
the batch never finished
last: expected "running" not to be "running"
```

| Throws | When |
| --- | --- |
| `ASSERTION_FAILED` | The deadline passed without a passing sample |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | `timeout` or `interval` out of range, before the first read |
| `CANCELLED` | The attempt was cancelled or timed out |
| `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` | The phase that started the poll returned while it still ran |
| `HOOK_FAILED` | A `beforeAll` or `afterAll` hook returned while its poll still ran |

<Note>
Await every poll. A poll belongs to the phase that started it: the test body
(with its fixtures and `beforeEach` hooks), one `afterEach` hook or fixture
teardown, or one `beforeAll` or `afterAll` hook. When that phase returns
while the poll still runs, the poll is cancelled and the phase fails with
`STEP_NOT_AWAITED` at the line of the call, whether or not the poll would
have passed. A body that threw keeps its own error and records this one
under `secondaryErrors`, and a suite hook reports it as `HOOK_FAILED`.
</Note>

A poll never fails a later test: a poll started by work its phase left
running, such as a body past its timeout, is cancelled before its first
read.

## Behavior

Rules that apply across the matcher groups.

### Timeouts and failures

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Default timeout | [`config.assertionTimeout`](/reference/config#assertiontimeout) |
| Override | `{ timeout }` in milliseconds, on every locator and `browser` matcher |
| Unknown option | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; see [Option validation](#option-validation) |
| Failure code | `ASSERTION_FAILED`, exit code 1 |

### Negation

`.not` inverts a matcher. A negated matcher passes only once the negation
has held:

- It passes after 1000 ms of continuous truth.
- When `{ timeout }` is shorter than 1000 ms, it passes at the deadline if the
  negation held for the whole budget.
- The window counts from the moment the first read that saw the negation
  started, so a slow read counts toward it.

### Strictness

- A positive locator matcher requires exactly one match. The exceptions are
  `toHaveCount` and the list form of `toHaveText` and `toContainText`.
- Zero matches keep polling until the timeout.
- Multiple matches fail immediately with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`.
- `toBeHidden`, `toBeVisible({ visible: false })`,
  `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`, negated visibility, and negated
  `toBeAttached` accept zero matches.
- For those, and for `waitFor({ state: 'detached' })` and `'hidden'`, a
  locator under a frame that is not in the document is zero matches rather
  than a wait for the frame.

### Text matching

- Text comparison is normalized: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
  and each run of whitespace collapses to one space.
- `toHaveText` and `toContainText` read the same rendered text as
  [`textContent()`](/reference/screen#locator-reads), `innerText` on the web.
- A `TextMatch` string matches exactly. A `RegExp` uses its own source and
  flags. Anything else, such as a predicate function, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- `ignoreCase: true` on `toHaveText`, `toContainText`, `toHaveAccessibleName`,
  and the value form of `toHaveAttribute` compares a string case-insensitively
  and adds the `i` flag to a `RegExp`; `ignoreCase: false` removes it.
- `toHaveAttribute(name, value)` compares like `toHaveText`, after
  normalization.
- [`toHaveValue`](#tohavevalue) is the exception: it compares a value as it
  is.

### Secure fields

A secure field, such as a password input, is never judged: the engine
withholds its value and text.

| Matcher | On a secure field |
| --- | --- |
| `toHaveValue`, `toHaveText`, `toContainText` | `POLICY_DENIED`, like `inputValue()` and `textContent()`, negated or in list form too |
| `toHaveAttribute` | `POLICY_DENIED`, like `getAttribute()`, for every attribute name and negated too |
| `toHaveAccessibleName` and the state matchers | Answer as usual |

Reading the withheld value as `''` would pass a filled password field as
cleared, and reading the withheld `value` attribute as absent would pass
`not.toHaveAttribute('value')` on a password field that has one. Assert the
outcome of the fill, not the field.

### Option validation

- A matcher refuses any option key it does not take, and a flag that is not a
  boolean, with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before it reads the screen.
- Types catch these in TypeScript, but `e2e run` does not type-check, so the
  check runs for a JavaScript test or a computed option object too.
- Playwright options e2e does not implement, such as `indeterminate` on
  `toBeChecked` or `useInnerText` on `toHaveText`, fail this way instead of
  passing on the default.
- The boolean options Playwright gives these matchers (`checked`, `enabled`,
  `visible`, `attached`) work the same way here.

## Types

### `ExpectCall`, `SoftExpectCall`, and `Expect`

```ts
/** `T`, or `never` when `T` is `any`, so an `any` argument skips an overload. */
type NotAny<T> = 0 extends 1 & T ? never : T;

/** The `expect(actual)` call: a locator, `screen`, an engine fixture, or a value, told apart by the argument. */
export interface ExpectCall {
  <L extends Locator>(actual: NotAny<L>): AsyncExpectation;
  <S extends Screen>(actual: NotAny<S>): ScreenExpectation;
  <E extends object>(actual: Expectable<E>): E;
  <T>(actual: T, message?: string): ValueExpectation<T>;
}

/** The `expect.soft(actual)` call: `expect(actual)` whose failures are kept instead of thrown. */
export interface SoftExpectCall {
  <L extends Locator>(actual: NotAny<L>): AsyncExpectation;
  <S extends Screen>(actual: NotAny<S>): ScreenExpectation;
  <E extends object>(actual: Expectable<E>): E;
  <T>(actual: T, message?: string): SoftValueExpectation<T>;
}

/** The `expect` entry: the call, `expect.poll`, `expect.soft`, and the asymmetric matchers. */
export interface Expect extends ExpectCall {
  /** Re-reads a value until the chosen matcher holds or `timeout` passes. */
  poll<T>(read: () => T | Promise<T>, options?: PollOptions): PollExpectation<T>;
  /** The same matchers, a failure kept on the attempt instead of thrown; the attempt fails once the body has settled. */
  readonly soft: SoftExpectCall;
  any(sample: Class | typeof BigInt | typeof Symbol): AsymmetricMatcher;
  anything(): AsymmetricMatcher;
  objectContaining(sample: object): AsymmetricMatcher;
  arrayContaining(sample: readonly unknown[]): AsymmetricMatcher;
  stringContaining(sample: string): AsymmetricMatcher;
  stringMatching(sample: string | RegExp): AsymmetricMatcher;
}
```

### `AsyncExpectation` and `TextMatcherOptions`

```ts
/**
 * The locator matchers. An option a matcher does not take, or a flag that is
 * not a boolean, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before the first read.
 */
export interface AsyncExpectation {
  /** Inverts the matcher. A negated matcher passes after 1000 ms of continuous truth. */
  readonly not: AsyncExpectation;
  /** Waits for visibility; `visible: false` waits for hidden or absent state, as `toBeHidden`. */
  toBeVisible(options?: { visible?: boolean; timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for hidden or absent state. */
  toBeHidden(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for one match to exist, visible or not; `attached: false` waits for none. */
  toBeAttached(options?: { attached?: boolean; timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for enabled state; `enabled: false` waits for disabled state. */
  toBeEnabled(options?: { enabled?: boolean; timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for disabled state. */
  toBeDisabled(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for checked state; `checked: false` waits for unchecked state. */
  toBeChecked(options?: { checked?: boolean; timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for selected state. */
  toBeSelected(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for expanded state. */
  toBeExpanded(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for focused state. */
  toBeFocused(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for exact normalized text; a list waits for exactly that many matches, each with its entry's text, in order. */
  toHaveText(expected: TextMatch, options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  toHaveText(expected: readonly TextMatch[], options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for contained normalized text; a list waits for each entry to be contained by a distinct match, in order, extra matches allowed. */
  toContainText(expected: TextMatch, options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  toContainText(expected: readonly TextMatch[], options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for a form control's value, compared as it is. */
  toHaveValue(expected: TextMatch, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for the attribute to be present; with `value`, for it to match. */
  toHaveAttribute(name: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  toHaveAttribute(name: string, value: TextMatch, options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for an exact match count. */
  toHaveCount(expected: number, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for an accessible name. */
  toHaveAccessibleName(expected: TextMatch, options?: TextMatcherOptions): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for the one match to look like its stored screenshot; see [Screenshot matchers](#screenshot-matchers). */
  toHaveScreenshot(name: string, options?: ScreenshotOptions): Promise<void>;
  toHaveScreenshot(options?: ScreenshotOptions): Promise<void>;
}

/** Options of a locator matcher that compares text. */
export interface TextMatcherOptions {
  /** Compares a string case-insensitively; on a RegExp, `true` adds the `i` flag and `false` removes it. */
  ignoreCase?: boolean;
  /** Assertion budget in milliseconds. */
  timeout?: number;
}
```

### `ScreenExpectation` and `ScreenshotOptions`

```ts
export interface ScreenExpectation {
  /** Inverts the matcher: waits for the screen to differ from its stored screenshot. */
  readonly not: ScreenExpectation;
  /** Waits for the screen to look like its stored screenshot, `name` or one named after the test. */
  toHaveScreenshot(name: string, options?: ScreenshotOptions): Promise<void>;
  toHaveScreenshot(options?: ScreenshotOptions): Promise<void>;
}

export interface ScreenshotOptions {
  /** How far one pixel's color may drift and still count as the same, from 0 (exact) to 1. Default `0.2`. */
  threshold?: number;
  /** How many pixels may differ. Default `0`. */
  maxDiffPixels?: number;
  /** What share of the pixels may differ, from 0 to 1. Default `0`. */
  maxDiffPixelRatio?: number;
  /** Locators painted over before comparing, for content that changes from run to run. */
  mask?: readonly Locator[];
  /** Color of the `mask` boxes, `#rrggbb`. Default `#ff00ff`. */
  maskColor?: string;
  /** Assertion budget in milliseconds. */
  timeout?: number;
}
```

### `BrowserExpectation`

```ts
export interface BrowserExpectation {
  /** Inverts the matcher. */
  readonly not: BrowserExpectation;
  /** Waits for the current URL to match; `ignoreCase` compares a string case-insensitively and adds the `i` flag to a RegExp, `false` removes it. */
  toHaveURL(expected: string | RegExp, options?: { ignoreCase?: boolean; timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for the current title to match. */
  toHaveTitle(expected: TextMatch, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits for the target's `class` attribute to match: a string is the whole normalized class list, a RegExp is tested against it. */
  toHaveClass(target: Locator, expected: TextMatch, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void>;
}
```

### `ValueExpectation`

```ts
export interface ValueExpectation<T> {
  /** Inverts the matcher. */
  readonly not: NegatedValueExpectation<T>;
  /** Compares with Object.is. */
  toBe(expected: T): void;
  /** Performs recursive structural equality; `undefined` properties are ignored and class types are not compared. */
  toEqual(expected: unknown): void;
  /** Requires every property of `expected` to match recursively; extra properties on the value are fine, arrays must match element-wise with equal length. */
  toMatchObject(expected: object): void;
  /** Requires a truthy value. */
  toBeTruthy(): void;
  /** Requires a falsy value. */
  toBeFalsy(): void;
  /** Requires null. */
  toBeNull(): void;
  /** Requires undefined. */
  toBeUndefined(): void;
  /** Requires any value but undefined; null passes. */
  toBeDefined(): void;
  /** Requires a `length` property equal to `expected`: a string, an array, or anything array-like. */
  toHaveLength(expected: number): void;
  /** Requires the property at `path` to exist; with `expected`, to equal it by `toEqual` rules. */
  toHaveProperty(path: PropertyPath, ...expected: [] | [expected: unknown]): void;
  /** Requires string or collection containment. */
  toContain(expected: unknown): void;
  /** Requires a string or regexp match. */
  toMatch(expected: string | RegExp): void;
  /** Requires a numeric lower bound. */
  toBeGreaterThan(expected: number): void;
  /** Requires a numeric lower bound, inclusive. */
  toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected: number): void;
  /** Requires a numeric upper bound. */
  toBeLessThan(expected: number): void;
  /** Requires a numeric upper bound, inclusive. */
  toBeLessThanOrEqual(expected: number): void;
  /** Requires a number within `10 ** -digits / 2` of `expected`; `digits` defaults to 2. */
  toBeCloseTo(expected: number, digits?: number): void;
  /**
   * Requires the value to pass a synchronous Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot,
   * ArkType, ...) and returns the schema's output, typed:
   * `const users = expect(await response.json()).toMatchSchema(Users)`.
   * A schema that validates asynchronously is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
   */
  toMatchSchema<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>;
}

/** `expect(value).not`: every value matcher inverted, none returning a value; `Back` is what `.not` returns to. */
export type NegatedValueExpectation<T, Back = ValueExpectation<T>> = {
  readonly not: Back;
} & {
  readonly [K in Exclude<keyof ValueExpectation<T>, 'not'>]: (...args: Parameters<ValueExpectation<T>[K]>) => void;
};

/** `expect.soft(value)`: the value matchers, with `toMatchSchema` returning `undefined` after a kept failure. */
export type SoftValueExpectation<T> = Omit<ValueExpectation<T>, 'toMatchSchema' | 'not'> & {
  readonly not: NegatedValueExpectation<T, SoftValueExpectation<T>>;
  toMatchSchema<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema> | undefined;
};

/** A class, abstract or not: what `expect.any` takes. */
export type Class = abstract new (...args: never[]) => unknown;

/** A property path for `toHaveProperty`: dotted (`'user.address.city'`) or one key per element (`['user', 'address', 'city']`). */
export type PropertyPath = string | readonly (string | number)[];
```

### `AsymmetricMatcher`

```ts
/**
 * A stand-in for a value inside `toEqual`, `toMatchObject`, `toContain`, and
 * `toHaveProperty`: `expect.any(Number)` in place of a number,
 * `expect.objectContaining({ id: 1 })` in place of a record. The structural
 * matchers ask it whether a value matches instead of comparing.
 */
export interface AsymmetricMatcher {
  /** Whether `other` satisfies the matcher. */
  asymmetricMatch(other: unknown): boolean;
  /** The matcher's name, `ObjectContaining`; a failure message adds the sample. */
  toString(): string;
}
```

### `PollOptions` and `PollExpectation`

```ts
export interface PollOptions {
  /** Deadline in milliseconds. Default 5000. */
  timeout?: number;
  /** Pause between reads in milliseconds. Default 100. */
  interval?: number;
  /** Extra line in the timeout error, after the matcher line. */
  message?: string;
}

/**
 * The asynchronous form of every `ValueExpectation<T>` matcher: the same
 * names and parameters, each resolving once the re-read value passes;
 * `toMatchSchema` resolves to the schema's output for the passing read.
 * Derived from `ValueExpectation<T>` so the two cannot drift.
 */
export type PollExpectation<T> = {
  readonly not: NegatedPollExpectation<T>;
} & {
  readonly [K in Exclude<keyof ValueExpectation<T>, 'not' | 'toMatchSchema'>]: (
    ...args: Parameters<ValueExpectation<T>[K]>
  ) => Promise<void>;
} & {
  toMatchSchema<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): Promise<StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>>;
};

/** `expect.poll(read).not`: every poll matcher inverted, none resolving to a value. */
export type NegatedPollExpectation<T> = {
  readonly not: PollExpectation<T>;
} & {
  readonly [K in Exclude<keyof ValueExpectation<T>, 'not'>]: (...args: Parameters<ValueExpectation<T>[K]>) => Promise<void>;
};
```

name: examples

# Every example under examples/ on every platform it supports, each night,
# against the packages built from main rather than the npm releases its
# package.json names: a change that breaks a user's first project shows up
# the next morning, before a release ships it. with-limrun is left out: it
# leases paid hosted devices.
#
# The examples commit no lockfile, so every dependency besides ours resolves
# the way a fresh project's would; a new Vite, Expo, Gradle plugin, or Flutter
# release that breaks a demo fails here too. The deterministic tests and the
# agent tests both run, the agent tests with real model calls (nothing is
# recorded for them), and every test gets one retry: a test that needed it
# reads as flaky instead of failing the night.
#
# The `summary` job posts one Slack message for the whole run: a line per
# example and platform saying how far it got (setup, app build, tests) and
# what its report counted. It needs the SLACK_EXAMPLES_NIGHTLY_WEBHOOK_URL
# secret, an incoming webhook. Nothing here gates a pull request: no
# pull_request or merge_group trigger, and no gate job.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 23 * * *'
      timezone: Europe/Warsaw
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  # The repository's own runs are not usage: the CLI sends no telemetry from CI here.
  E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Builds the packages once and packs the three an example installs, so every
  # job below installs the same main build. Only this repository runs it:
  # GitHub turns a fork's schedules off, but a fork's owner can still
  # dispatch the workflow, and it would spend their runners and model key.
  # Every example job needs this one, so on a fork they all skip with it.
  pack:
    if: ${{ github.repository == 'tester-army/e2e' }}
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      # `missing` tells the summary a missing key, not the build, stopped the night.
      credential: ${{ steps.credential.outputs.credential }}
    steps:
      # Without a key the agent tests skip, and a night of skips reads as green.
      - name: Require model credential
        id: credential
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "credential=missing" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::error::AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY is not set for this repository. The examples' agent tests need it."
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build
      - name: Pack
        run: |
          pnpm --filter e2e pack --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/packed/e2e.tgz"
          pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web pack --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/packed/web.tgz"
          pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile pack --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/packed/mobile.tgz"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: packed
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/packed
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  # The runner starts each app's dev server; Expo's is `expo start --web`.
  web:
    name: web ${{ matrix.id }}
    needs: pack
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { id: vite, name: Vite, tests: examples/with-vite, target: '' }
          - { id: next, name: Next.js, tests: examples/with-next, target: '' }
          - { id: astro, name: Astro, tests: examples/with-astro, target: '' }
          - { id: expo, name: Expo, tests: examples/with-expo, target: web }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Install the packages
        id: setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/example-packages
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
      # The runner downloads its own Chromium on first use; the system
      # libraries it links against need root.
      - name: Chromium system dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
        run: npx playwright-core install-deps chromium
      - name: Run the tests
        id: test
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: npx e2e run --retries 1 ${TARGET:+--target "$TARGET"}
      - name: Record the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        env: &outcome-env
          OUTCOME_ID: ${{ matrix.id }}
          OUTCOME_NAME: ${{ matrix.name }}
          # The setup, build, and test steps' outcomes; web jobs have no build step.
          STEPS: ${{ toJSON(steps) }}
          TESTS_DIR: ${{ matrix.tests }}
          # The job id: web, android, or ios.
          PLATFORM: ${{ github.job }}
        run: &record-outcome |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/outcome"
          node -e '
            const env = process.env;
            const steps = JSON.parse(env.STEPS);
            const step = (id) => steps[id]?.outcome ?? "";
            const outcome = {
              id: env.OUTCOME_ID, name: env.OUTCOME_NAME, platform: env.PLATFORM,
              job: `${env.PLATFORM} ${env.OUTCOME_ID}`,
              setup: step("setup"), build: step("build"), test: step("test"),
            };
            require("node:fs").writeFileSync(`${env.RUNNER_TEMP}/outcome/outcome.json`, JSON.stringify(outcome));
          '
          if [ -f "$TESTS_DIR/.e2e/report.json" ]; then cp "$TESTS_DIR/.e2e/report.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/outcome/"; fi
      - name: Upload the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: outcome-web-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/outcome
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Upload the results
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: results-web-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ matrix.tests }}/.e2e/results
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  # Each app builds before the emulator starts, then installs on it. Every
  # Android toolchain here (Gradle, Flutter, .NET) needs a JDK 17.
  android:
    name: android ${{ matrix.id }}
    needs: pack
    # x64 Blacksmith runners expose KVM, which the emulator needs.
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: compose
            name: Jetpack Compose
            project: examples/with-compose
            tests: examples/with-compose/e2e
            build: ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:assembleDebug
            app: app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
          - id: kmp
            name: Kotlin Multiplatform
            project: examples/with-kotlin-multiplatform
            tests: examples/with-kotlin-multiplatform/e2e
            build: ./gradlew --no-daemon :androidApp:assembleDebug
            app: androidApp/build/outputs/apk/debug/androidApp-debug.apk
          - id: flutter
            name: Flutter
            project: examples/with-flutter
            tests: examples/with-flutter/e2e
            toolchain: flutter
            build: flutter build apk
            app: build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk
          # A Debug build keeps its assemblies outside the APK unless told
          # otherwise, and an app whose data is cleared then exits at start.
          - id: maui
            name: .NET MAUI
            project: examples/with-maui
            tests: examples/with-maui/e2e
            toolchain: dotnet
            build: dotnet build -f net10.0-android -p:EmbedAssembliesIntoApk=true
            app: bin/Debug/net10.0-android/*-Signed.apk
          - id: expo
            name: Expo
            project: examples/with-expo
            tests: examples/with-expo
            # The default 2 GB Gradle heap runs out on React Native's release build.
            build: npx expo prebuild --platform android --no-install && (cd android && ./gradlew --no-daemon -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g assembleRelease)
            app: android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2.23.0
        if: ${{ matrix.toolchain == 'flutter' }}
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0
        if: ${{ matrix.toolchain == 'dotnet' }}
        with:
          dotnet-version: 10.0.x
      - name: MAUI workload
        if: ${{ matrix.toolchain == 'dotnet' }}
        run: dotnet workload install maui-android
      - name: Enable KVM for the emulator
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - name: Install the packages
        id: setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/example-packages
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
      - name: Build the app
        id: build
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.project }}
        env:
          BUILD: ${{ matrix.build }}
          APP: ${{ matrix.app }}
        run: &build-app |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$BUILD"
          # A glob in APP names the one file the build wrote.
          set -- $APP
          if [ "$#" -ne 1 ] || [ ! -e "$1" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected one app at $APP, found: $*"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "APP_PATH=$PWD/$1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      # The emulator lives for this step only and runs each `script` line in
      # its own shell.
      - name: Run the tests
        id: test
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 36
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          profile: pixel_7
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim -no-metrics
          disable-animations: true
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
          script: |
            adb install -r "$APP_PATH"
            npx e2e run --target android --retries 1
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
      - name: Record the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        env: *outcome-env
        run: *record-outcome
      - name: Upload the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: outcome-android-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/outcome
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Upload the results
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: results-android-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ matrix.tests }}/.e2e/results
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  # One simulator per job, on the newest iOS runtime the runner image has.
  # The Mac runner is Apple silicon, so each app builds for arm64 alone: the
  # Kotlin Multiplatform framework has no x86_64 simulator slice to link.
  ios:
    name: ios ${{ matrix.id }}
    needs: pack
    runs-on: blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 75
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: swiftui
            name: SwiftUI
            project: examples/with-swiftui
            tests: examples/with-swiftui/e2e
            build: >-
              xcodebuild build -project HelloApp.xcodeproj -scheme HelloApp -configuration Debug
              -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ARCHS=arm64
            app: build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/HelloApp.app
          # The Xcode build runs Gradle for the shared Kotlin code, so it needs the JDK.
          - id: kmp
            name: Kotlin Multiplatform
            project: examples/with-kotlin-multiplatform
            tests: examples/with-kotlin-multiplatform/e2e
            toolchain: java
            build: >-
              xcodebuild build -project iosApp/iosApp.xcodeproj -scheme iosApp -configuration Debug
              -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ARCHS=arm64
            app: build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/iosApp.app
          - id: flutter
            name: Flutter
            project: examples/with-flutter
            tests: examples/with-flutter/e2e
            toolchain: flutter
            build: flutter build ios --simulator
            app: build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app
          # The MAUI iOS workload pins the Xcode it was built against; the
          # runner image's newer Xcode builds the app fine.
          - id: maui
            name: .NET MAUI
            project: examples/with-maui
            tests: examples/with-maui/e2e
            toolchain: dotnet
            build: dotnet build -f net10.0-ios -p:RuntimeIdentifier=iossimulator-arm64 -p:ValidateXcodeVersion=false
            app: bin/Debug/net10.0-ios/iossimulator-arm64/WithMaui.app
          # The prebuild names the workspace and scheme after the app's slug.
          - id: expo
            name: Expo
            project: examples/with-expo
            tests: examples/with-expo
            build: >-
              npx expo prebuild --platform ios &&
              xcodebuild build -workspace ios/withexpo.xcworkspace -scheme withexpo -configuration Release
              -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ARCHS=arm64
            app: build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/withexpo.app
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
      # Booting takes a minute or two; it runs while the app builds.
      - name: Boot a simulator
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PICK="$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j | node -e '
            const payload = JSON.parse(require("node:fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8"));
            const runtimes = Object.entries(payload.devices)
              .filter(([runtime]) => runtime.includes("SimRuntime.iOS-"))
              .sort(([a], [b]) => b.localeCompare(a, undefined, { numeric: true }));
            for (const [runtime, list] of runtimes) {
              const pick = list.find((d) => d.name === "iPhone 17 Pro") ?? list.find((d) => d.name.startsWith("iPhone"));
              if (pick) { process.stdout.write(`${pick.udid} ${runtime} ${pick.name}`); process.exit(0); }
            }
            process.exit(1);
          ')"
          UDID="${PICK%% *}"
          echo "booting ${PICK#* } ($UDID)"
          xcrun simctl boot "$UDID"
          echo "SIMULATOR_UDID=$UDID" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2.23.0

          cache: true
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0
        if: ${{ matrix.toolchain == 'dotnet' }}
        with:
          dotnet-version: 10.0.x
      # Restore reads every target framework in the project, so an iOS build
      # still needs the Android workload on macOS (NETSDK1147 without it).
      # Workload set 10.0.402.1 binds iOS 27.1 and needs Xcode 27.1, which the

      - name: Install the packages
        id: setup

      - name: Build the app
        id: build
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.project }}
        env:
          BUILD: ${{ matrix.build }}
          APP: ${{ matrix.app }}
        run: *build-app
      - name: Run the tests
        id: test
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.tests }}
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$SIMULATOR_UDID"
          xcrun simctl install "$SIMULATOR_UDID" "$APP_PATH"
          npx e2e run --target ios --retries 1
      - name: Record the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        env: *outcome-env
        run: *record-outcome
      - name: Upload the outcome
        if: ${{ always() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: outcome-ios-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/outcome
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Upload the results
        if: ${{ failure() }}

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: results-ios-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ matrix.tests }}/.e2e/results

---
title: Reporters
description: Receive run events and publish results with a custom reporter.
icon: "file-lines"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/reference/reporters.png?v=6f74d2a2a5"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/reference/reporters.png?v=6f74d2a2a5"
---

A reporter receives the run's events as they happen and the finished run
once its report is written. `reporters` in `e2e.config.ts` lists built-in
reporters by id beside reporter objects.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { github } from '@e2e-dev/github';

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' } }],
  reporters: ['list', 'junit', github()],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

## Reference

### Built-in reporters

| Reporter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`list`](#list) | Terminal progress and run summary |
| [`json`](#json) | Report document to stdout |
| [`junit`](#junit) | Writes `<output>/junit.xml` |
| [`markdown`](#markdown) | Writes `<output>/summary.md` |
| [`github()`](#github) | Pull request comment and job summary |

| Throws | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | `reporters` is not an array. |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | An id other than `list`, `json`, `junit`, or `markdown`. |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | An entry that is neither an id nor an object with a `name` and at least one handler. |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | `json` together with `list`. |

#### `list`

Renders terminal progress, failures, and the run summary.

```ts
reporters: ['list'], // default
```

- It renders the same events [`onEvent`](#onevent) receives.
- The [summary rows](#onrunfinished) reporters return print under its
  summary.

#### `json`

Prints the report document to stdout.

```ts
reporters: ['json'],
```

#### `junit`

Writes `junit.xml` beside the report.

```ts
reporters: ['list', 'junit'],
```

- It reads `run.report`, writes `junit.xml` beside `run.reportPath`, and
  returns one row naming the file. It is the smallest complete example of a
  reporter.
- A second Ctrl-C still lets it write its file, so no file from the previous
  run is left beside the new report.

#### `markdown`

Writes `summary.md` beside the report.

```ts
reporters: ['list', 'markdown'],
```

It does what `junit` does, second Ctrl-C included, with `summary.md` and
through [`renderMarkdownReport`](#rendermarkdownreport).

<a id="rendermarkdownreport" />

##### `renderMarkdownReport`

Renders a report as the Markdown page the `markdown` reporter writes, so
your own reporter can post the same page elsewhere.

```ts
import { renderMarkdownReport, type Reporter } from 'e2e';

const reporter: Reporter = {
  name: 'wiki',
  async onRunFinished(run) {
    const page = renderMarkdownReport(run.report, { traces: run.traces });
    await fetch('https://wiki.example.test/runs', { method: 'POST', body: page });
  },
};
```

- `traces` links each block to its trace page by result id.
- [`@e2e-dev/github`](/github) is that reporter for GitHub Actions.

#### `github()`

`@e2e-dev/github` posts the run as one pull request comment from GitHub
Actions, keeps it current on reruns, and writes the same text to the job
summary.

```ts
import { github } from '@e2e-dev/github';

const reporter = github({ key: 'chromium' });
```

- `key` tells one job's comment apart from another's when the workflow, job,
  and project are the same, as in a matrix. Without it, matrix replicas of
  one job share a comment, and the last one to finish wins. Never use the
  run id: a rerun must find the old comment. The key also names the comment
  in its headline: `e2e chromium: 77 passed`.
- It reads the token, the event, and the repository when the run finishes,
  never when the config loads.
- With `--last-failed`, it folds the rerun into [`lastRun`](#onrunfinished)
  to show both runs as one comment.
- Setup and permissions are on [Pull request comments](/github).

### Custom reporters

A reporter object has a `name` and at least one handler. Use `onEvent` for
live progress and `onRunFinished` to process the final report and artifacts.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig, Reporter } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';

const upload: Reporter = {
  name: 'upload',
  async onRunFinished(run) {
    const response = await fetch('https://example.test/runs', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(run.report),
    });
    const { url } = (await response.json()) as { url: string };
    return [{ label: 'Results', text: url }];
  },
};

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'localhost:3000' } }],
  reporters: ['list', upload],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

| Member | Type |
| --- | --- |
| [`name`](#name) | `string` |
| [`onEvent`](#onevent) | `(event: RunEvent) => void` |
| [`onRunFinished`](#onrunfinished) | `(run, signal) => Promise<…>` |

```ts
interface Reporter {
  readonly name: string;
  onEvent?(event: RunEvent): void;
  onRunFinished?(run: FinishedRun, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ReporterSummary | void>;
}
```

Cached steps expose `cache.recordedBy: { provider, model }` in `report.json`
and on the trace page when the recording has it. Older recordings omit it.
The console prints `replayed · recorded with provider/model` only when that
identity differs from the configured model. It stays quiet for multi-agent
runs and for pinned agents whose model is not in the run header.

#### `name`

The reporter's label in diagnostics. Required and non-empty.

```ts
name: 'upload',
```

#### `onEvent`

Receives every run event as it happens, as plain JSON.

```ts
onEvent(event) {
  switch (event.type) {
    case 'test-finished':
      console.log(event.result.test.title, event.result.status);
      break;
    default:
  }
},
```

[Events](#events) lists them.

<Note>
`onEvent` must not block and must not throw. Do slow work in
`onRunFinished`. A throw quarantines the reporter for the rest of the run and
prints one line on stderr naming the reporter, the event type, and the error.
The run's outcome is unchanged.
</Note>

#### `onRunFinished`

Runs once the report is written and the terminal summary prints, with the
finished run and an `AbortSignal`.

```ts
async onRunFinished(run, signal) {
  await fetch('https://example.test/runs', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(run.report), signal });
  return [{ label: 'Results', text: 'https://example.test/runs/0192c' }];
},
```

```ts
interface FinishedRun {
  readonly report: Report;                 // the report-1 document, as written
  readonly status: RunStatus;              // report.run.status
  readonly exitCode: RunExitCode;
  readonly projectRoot: string;            // what the terminal shows paths relative to
  readonly reportPath: string | undefined; // absent when the write failed
  readonly artifactsRoot: string;          // what the report's artifact paths are relative to
  readonly aiTracePath: string | undefined;
  readonly traces: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;      // result id -> its trace page, from the project root
  readonly lastRun?: Report;               // with --last-failed, the report the rerun selected from
}

type ReporterSummary = readonly { label: string; text: string }[];
```

- All reporters run concurrently, each with a one-minute deadline.
- A timeout, exception, or invalid return value is reported on stderr. The
  run's status, exit code, and report do not change.
- One Ctrl-C still lets reporters finish. A second Ctrl-C stops waiting for
  them, except [`junit`](#junit) and [`markdown`](#markdown).
- `signal` aborts when the budget runs out or the run is forced to stop.
- The runner writes the trace pages, `results/<test>/trace.md`, before it
  calls `onRunFinished`.

<Note>
Hand `signal` to every request and timer. The CLI exits without waiting for
a reporter it abandoned, cutting off what it still does; under
[`e2e/runner`](/reference/runner), that work keeps your process alive.
</Note>

##### Summary rows

The rows a reporter resolves with print under the `list` summary, in the
same layout as its own rows. The `json` reporter does not carry them.

```
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  6 passed (6)
     Start at  14:02:11
     Duration  8.41s

        JUnit  .e2e/junit.xml
      Results  https://example.test/runs/0192c…
```

##### Artifacts

- Artifact paths in the report are POSIX paths relative to `artifactsRoot`.
- `path`, `size`, and `sha256` are optional: an artifact whose file never
  appeared, or that a redaction withheld, is recorded without them. Check for
  `path` before reading.
- A video a hosted service keeps has an `http(s)` `url` in place of `path`.

##### Reruns with `--last-failed`

- The rerun's own report lists the tests it left out as unselected. A
  reporter that keeps one place current, the way `@e2e-dev/github` keeps a
  pull request comment, folds the rerun into `lastRun` to show both runs as
  one.
- A test the rerun owed but another filter left out is in the rerun's
  `run.carried`. It holds the test's last result, the serial group its
  attempts live on, and the `beforeAll` or `afterAll` failure whose scope
  holds it, from whichever earlier run reported them.
- A fold shows the carried result in place of the unselected one and counts
  a carried failure or hook error against the outcome.
- The artifacts both reports name are on disk under `artifactsRoot`.

<a id="test-filters" />
##### Test filters

- A test a [test filter](/filters) left out is an unselected result with
  `skip.cause` `filtered` and `skip.filter` naming the filter.
- `run.filters` holds one record per filter that was called, in order:
  `name`, `candidates`, `excluded` (the tests left out once serial groups
  took back their members), `note` (cut to 1024 characters; for a filter
  that failed or timed out, the warning saying why), and `outcome`, set
  when the filter left nothing out: `failed` when it threw or returned an
  invalid result, `timed-out` when it ran past 5 minutes. A filter left with
  no tests is not called and has no record.
- Once the filters have decided, `run.changes` holds the change they
  judged, by counts: `base` (the merge base), `files`, and `skipped` (why
  no filter ran, such as `no files changed since abc1234`). It is present when filters are configured and
  the run passed `--changed-since`, except under `e2e explore`, on
  `--watch` reruns, and when the run ends before the filters decide. On
  `--last-failed`, or with no tests to judge, it holds `skipped` alone.
- A failure while the filters decide, such as `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE` for a
  ref that names no commit, is in `run.errors` with `phase` `filter`. A
  malformed `changedSince` has `phase` `config`.

## Events

`onEvent` receives one of these facts. Each event also has a sequence
number, `seq`, and an ISO timestamp, `at`.

```ts
type RunEventFact =
  | { type: 'run-started'; runId; projectId; projectRoot; artifactsRoot; ci; targets; agents?; model?; judge? }
  | { type: 'plan'; total; files: { file; target; tests }[] }
  | { type: 'notice'; target; message }
  | { type: 'output'; target; pair; stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'; text }
  | { type: 'setup'; step: SetupStep; state: 'started' }
  | { type: 'setup'; step: SetupStep; state: 'finished'; durationMs; outcome?: 'reused' | 'failed' | 'timed-out' }
  | { type: 'test-started'; testId; agent; repeat; title; file; serialId; target }
  | { type: 'step'; testId; agent; repeat; target; progress: StepProgress }
  | { type: 'test-finished'; result: RunEventResult }
  | { type: 'serial-group'; group: SerialGroupRecord }
  | { type: 'explore'; progress: ExploreProgress }
  | { type: 'run-error'; error: SerializedError }
  | { type: 'run-interrupted'; mode: 'graceful' | 'forced' }
  | { type: 'run-stopped'; failures; limit }
  | { type: 'run-finished'; status; exitCode; reportPath?; aiTracePath?; traces? };
```

- `run-started` comes first and `run-finished` last.
- `judge` on `run-started` is the run agent's judge model, present only when
  judgments use a model other than `model`.
- `setup` brackets the work before the tests start. Its `step.kind` is
  `collect`, `filter` (one [test filter](/filters), by its `name`),
  `prepare`, `service`, or `app`. `outcome` is `reused` when a service or
  app command attached to a process already serving its URL, `failed` when
  a filter threw or returned an invalid result, and `timed-out` when a
  filter ran past 5 minutes.
- A `notice` names what its line is about in `target`: a target, `app`,
  `collect`, `filter` for a test filter's progress and summary, or `run`.
- `output` is one write a test made to stdout or stderr; `pair` names the
  test running at the time and is undefined between tests.
- `test-finished` carries the full result record, including every attempt's
  artifacts.
- `explore` appears only in an `e2e explore` run: `started`, `planning`,
  `step-started`, `step-finished`, `finding`, and `finished`. The record of
  all of it is `run.explore` in the report.
- New event types are added over time. Handle the types you know and ignore
  the rest; leave the `default` branch of a `switch` empty.

### Tests and attempts

- A test pinned to several agents starts and finishes once per agent, so key
  running state by test id, target, and agent together.
- Ordinary tests emit `test-started` once for that combination. Serial
  members emit it on each group attempt they execute.
- Use step progress [identity](#step-progress) to distinguish retries.
- An attempt that fails before any step emits no step progress and appears
  in the final result.

<Note>
Secrets are redacted before events are built. Error messages are only
stripped of control characters, so treat them as untrusted.
</Note>

### Step progress

The `phase` field describes step progress:

- `start` and `end` mark the step's boundaries.
- `event` reports a completed model turn, tool call, or observation.
- `activity` reports work starting: `observe`, `action`, or `model`.
- `replay` reports when replay from the cache starts or returns control to
  the agent.

```ts
type StepProgress = (
  | { phase: 'start'; kind: StepKind; api: string; label: string }
  | {
      phase: 'end';
      kind: StepKind;
      api: string;
      label: string;
      status: 'passed' | 'failed' | 'blocked' | 'timed-out' | 'cancelled';
      durationMs: number;
      modelCalls: number;
      error?: SerializedError;
      explanation?: string;
    }
  | { phase: 'event'; api: string; event: StepEvent }
  | { phase: 'activity'; api: string; activity: 'observe' | 'model' | 'action' }
  | { phase: 'replay'; api: string; active: boolean }
) & { identity?: StepProgressIdentity };
```

An `end` phase's `error` and `explanation` are redacted. Keep its `status`,
including `blocked` and `cancelled`. Do not treat every non-passed step as a
product failure.

Every step phase the runner emits includes `progress.identity`:

```ts
{ attemptId: string; attemptIndex: number; stepId: string; stepIndex: number }
```

- The IDs match the final report. Both indexes start at zero.
- A retry has a new attempt ID and a higher attempt index; its step indexes
  start again at zero.
- Serial-group members share the group's attempt ID and index. Each
  member's step IDs stay distinct.
- Use `stepId` to match start, activity, event, replay, and end phases,
  including nested steps.
- `identity` is optional in the type so a reporter can also accept older
  streams.

## What `--reporter` does to reporter objects

`--reporter` replaces only the built-in reporters; configured reporter
objects still run.

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npx e2e run --reporter list,junit
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm exec e2e run --reporter list,junit
```

```bash bun
bunx e2e run --reporter list,junit
```
</CodeGroup>

- A config with only reporter objects has no built-in terminal output.

## Where a reporter runs

Handlers run in the runner process. Workers also load the config, so
reporter construction must have no side effects.

- Read tokens and start requests inside handlers.
- Adding a reporter leaves [cached traces](/cache#what-must-match) valid.

## Types

`Reporter`, `FinishedRun`, `ReporterSummary`, `Report`, `RunEvent`, and
`RunEventOf` are exported from the main entrypoint, and so is
`renderMarkdownReport(report, options)`.
